currentPublic.name: Aberrant Mind

sourceObject.name: Aberrant Mind
sourceObject.description: Your mind has been touched by alien intelligence.
sourceObject.effect: You can communicate telepathically with aberrations and have resistance to psychic damage.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Retain permanentINT15 prerequisite and resistance to psychic damage, subject to one same-type resistance. NEW while conscious, initiate one two-way telepathic conversation with one actual Aberration you perceive within60ft and line of effect. A brief message uses the ordinary free communication allowance on your own regular turn; an invited willing recipient may reply briefly without Action, including off-turn, without gaining another action. Both must know at least one language, but need not share one. No automatic type detection: choosing a non-Aberration produces no channel, not a diagnosis of why it failed. Recipient may refuse/end communication; you cannot read thoughts, memories, emotions or intentions, compel responses, or impersonate a voice. Maintain actual range/line of effect; loss ends the link. Silence/Deafened alone does not block purely mental speech, but Unconscious or explicit telepathy/mental-communication protection does. One channel at a time, no relay or shared senses. This grants no Aberration creature type, mutation activation or alien-origin fact.
workedCases: A willing Aberration knowing a different language may converse mentally within60ft; the feat reveals only its voluntary message.
A wall giving total cover ends the channel. Psychic resistance still applies to an otherwise legal psychic packet.

currentPublic.name: Acrobatic Mastery

sourceObject.name: Acrobatic Mastery
sourceObject.description: Disciplined balance turns a failed Acrobatics attempt into a practiced recovery.
sourceObject.effect: When you fail a Dexterity (Acrobatics) check, reroll it. You must use the new result. You regain this use after a long rest.
sourceObject.legacyEffect: Reroll failed Acrobatics check once per day
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: After an actual Dexterity (Acrobatics) task resolves to Failure or Critical Failure, or loses an opposed check including an initiating tie, and before its consequences commit, you may spend this feat's one long-rest use to reroll that complete check. NEW: reroll the entire original one- or two-d20 procedure with the same advantage/disadvantage state and the same modifiers. Keep the new result even if worse, recomputing natural shifts for a fixed DC; the opponent's already rolled total does not change. The reroll is part of the original paid action, not another movement attempt or escape Action. If another feature can alter a die, declare an eligible sequence before resolving it; this feat cannot reroll its own reroll, and no earlier result can be restored merely because the new result is worse. A purely Strength (Athletics) check does not qualify.
workedCases: DC 15, original natural 3 plus 3 gives Failure. Spend the use; the replacement natural 1 plus 3 becomes Critical Failure and must stand. The falling consequence occurs once after the replacement.
With advantage, original faces 2/4 and +3 fail DC 15. Replace both faces, not only the lower face. If replacement 1/8 gives 11, keep Failure; no second use is available until a completed long rest.

currentPublic.name: Actor

sourceObject.name: Actor
sourceObject.description: Skilled at mimicry and dramatics.
sourceObject.effect: You have advantage on Charisma (Deception) and Charisma (Performance) checks when trying to pass yourself off as a different person.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Gain advantage on actual Charisma (Deception) or Charisma (Performance) checks whose declared purpose is passing yourself off as a different person. NEW: the identity can be invented or real, but the chosen presentation must be physically possible with your actual appearance, voice, clothing, languages, knowledge and any separately active disguise or magic. Familiarity with a real person's observed traits supplies evidence for imitating those traits; it does not create an automatic perfect voice copy. The Director states what scrutiny the check resolves before rolling. A forged identity does not defeat an independent magical identification effect unless that effect actually calls for the qualifying check. This feat grants no kit, prepared disguise, extra preparation time, memories or understanding of an unlearned language. Disguise Expert's separate flat bonus may coexist only under the final feat-stacking decision; advantage itself never stacks.
workedCases: An actor who speaks the requested language and has observed a guard's manner can gain advantage on the actual Deception check to pass as that guard. The feat does not reveal the guard's private password.
A magical scan that directly reports the subject's actual identity without a Deception/Performance contest is not defeated by rolling with advantage on an unrelated conversation.

currentPublic.name: Animal Companion

sourceObject.name: Animal Companion
sourceObject.description: You have formed a bond with an animal.
sourceObject.effect: You gain an animal companion that follows your commands and fights alongside you.

currentPublic.operationalRules:
NEW ACQ-05 purchase/bond distinction: acquire Animal Companion once by committing one actual earned unspent feat opportunity while meeting its actual Animal Handling proficiency prerequisite and all other acquisition gates. Record that paid grant and its acquisition snapshot atomically. The animal and bonding hour are not conditions of purchasing the feat. Ownership begins at that commitment, with no companion and one unspent bond attempt under FS-06; it grants neither an animal nor an earlier completed Long Rest. Animal identity, matching template and any actually sourced sense choice belong to each bond record, not a permanently locked feat-purchase choice. The retained nonrepeatability/permanent-choice metadata does not prohibit the replacements expressly allowed here. Canceling a proposed purchase before commitment spends no opportunity. A completed purchase is not refunded or repeated because no animal is available, a bond attempt fails, or a bond later ends. Animal Companion ownership alone can satisfy Companion Training's printed parent alternative, but supplies neither its separate feat opportunity nor a creature on which to use it.

NEW ACQ-05 bond attempt: an owner of this feat with actual Animal Handling proficiency, no current feat bond, no other pending bond attempt, an unspent attempt and any required post-bond-ending Long Rest may select one already real, positive-HP living, willing/tamed, noncorrupted Beast with INT<7 fitting one of the three finite templates. The selected animal must have no incompatible existing bond, including another Animal Companion or Ranger bond. Finding, buying or taming it still needs actual lawful access and its real willing/tamed relationship to this owner; no animal, stocked shop, consent or charm is supplied. Preserve its actual identity, ordinary profile, current/maximum HP, conditions, injuries, native movement, breathing, custody and required template choices. In one ordered start event, recheck admission, reserve this owner and animal for the work, spend the one attempt, and begin the hour. Merely proposing a target or rejecting it before that event does not spend an attempt; it never reverses a previously completed feat purchase. Starting costs no RP, second feat opportunity or universal fee. An attempt cannot begin while an existing feat bond is retained; such a rejected proposal does not release or alter that bond.

Spend one uninterrupted hour of actual bonding work together at touch range. Keep the same owner and animal, actual access, the required proficiency and animal eligibility throughout the work and at completion; the owner must remain able to perform it. This is active work, not beneficial rest, and grants no extra work Watch, assistant shortcut, handover or overlapping incompatible task. Loss of required touch-range access, willing/tamed eligibility, qualifying body state, or the owner's ability to continue, including incapacitation, or voluntary abandonment terminates the attempt. Elapsed time, real losses and the spent attempt persist; no partial hour, resumed fraction or same-epoch retry is awarded. The prospective animal remains in its actual current ordinary state; no feat profile or command entitlement was installed. After a full lawful hour, atomically complete the one bond and apply the existing template/HP conversion to the animal's latest lawful ordinary state, using the owner's then-current governing statistics. No new bond check or success chance is added. Admission alone or an incomplete hour cannot establish a companion.

The initial allowance is one attempt at feat purchase. Each genuinely completed beneficial owner Long Rest thereafter sets the allowance to one, never adds a stored second attempt. Apply FS-06's actual rest limits and one elapsed clock: no reset from Short Rest, debt-only Rest, a repeated rest receipt, a scene, a new target, a new controller, a new day label or level growth. Do not credit active bonding or release work as rest. An invalid claimed completion record is evidence rejection, not an attempt or feat-payment refund: reconcile the real start/interruption/rest history. Missing history cannot be replaced by an assumed unspent allowance. One feat bond at a time. Use the template corresponding to the real animal's body/native movement; do not turn a dog into a bird or grant a new breathing mode. AC12+floor(ownerPB/2), maximumHP5+total owner level; template attack/ability/movement values are explicit NEW. At initial bond convert existing HP proportionally max(1,floor(newMax×oldHP/oldMax)); preserve actual conditions/injuries. Later maximum growth never heals, decreases clamp without damage. Ordinary legal healing works, but no Hit Dice/rest-refill is invented. Use one shared BA command within60ft while the animal can perceive you: in its attached phase after your regular turn, move and make its one attack or Dash/Disengage/Help/Dodge. No independent turn/Reaction; uncommanded move defensively and Dodge. The animal's HP-only chassis dies at0, producing its one actual corpse and ending the bond, with no Wound/death-save sequence; this is a feat-specific NEW rule, not generic animal law. NEW ACQ-05 replacement boundary: when an established feat bond ends through release or death, record that actual ending event. Before this owner begins any later feat bond, require a genuinely beneficial owner Long Rest whose completion is ordered after that event, as well as an available attempt, a real eligible living target and the full new hour. A rest completed before the ending event or an unused prior allowance cannot satisfy that replacement gate. A qualifying completion after the event is sufficient; no additional rule requires the whole rest to have started after it. Existing active-work/rest restrictions still apply. Replacement is a use of the already-owned nonrepeatable feat, not a second purchase. NEW explicit rebond interpretation: a previously released living animal may be selected again if it genuinely qualifies; it is a new bond to the same physical individual, not a new or refreshed animal. A dead animal never becomes eligible merely through rest, release, purchase or this procedure. Voluntary release requires the owner's one uninterrupted hour of actual release work. NEW ACQ-05 release boundary: record its start, but end the bond only on lawful completion; interruption or abandonment grants no partial-hour credit and leaves the existing bond intact unless an independent event already ended it. A fresh release hour may be begun while the bond still exists. Release consumes no bond attempt, feat opportunity or RP. It does not require a second target or borrow the bonding hour's touch-range requirement; actual owner capacity and uninterrupted work remain mandatory. At completion restore the same living animal's saved ordinary profile with the existing positive-current-HP ratio conversion, preserving its current conditions, injuries and actual custody without healing or refilling it. End the outgoing bond's control entitlement and unexecuted commands; preserve all already-spent body/actor allowances. No automatic transfer of custody or command occurs. Record this end for the post-ending Long-Rest gate. A creature cannot simultaneously have this and a Ranger bond, or two owners' Animal Companion bonds. NEW ACQ-05 correction of 'new paid acquisition': a transfer requires the outgoing bond to end through its actual lawful release/death/termination procedure, real lawful access/custody for the receiver, and the receiver's independently authorized new bond. An existing Animal Companion feat owner does not buy that nonrepeatable feat again; they spend their own available attempt and full hour and satisfy their own post-ending Long-Rest gate, if any. The sender's rest, feat ownership or spent attempt neither transfers nor resets the receiver's history. A receiver without this feat must first acquire it through their own actual eligible unspent opportunity, or use an independently acquired receiving engine; receiving the animal grants no feat or class feature. An actual Ranger Beast Companion route retains its own acquired Warder/class-level/selection gates, eligible-beast limits, 4 RP, one-hour touch procedure, once-per-beneficial-owner-Long-Rest allowance and native profile/lifecycle. This feat's no-RP route, release hour and attempt rules do not waive or redefine that class engine. A Ranger bond cannot be ended by invoking another engine's feat-release permission. No universal transfer payment, new animal, healing, additive chassis, second controller, extra phase or refunded body/resource budget is granted. Owner death ends the bond and, if the animal remains alive, restores its saved ordinary profile using the same positive-HP ratio conversion as release; a dead animal remains its actual corpse. Temporary owner incapacity prevents new commands but does not cancel a previously committed legal command; after that command, uncommanded phases remain defensive. This never supplies autonomous attacks.

Riding, bonding or transferring custody does not clone a turn, movement budget, Reaction, attack allowance, body or resource pool. An attached companion acts in its source-defined phase after the owner’s regular turn; a controlled mount uses EX58’s actual mounted-phase procedure. A body fitting both roles elects one compatible route before that round’s work, preserves all already-spent allowances and cannot switch routes to gain a second phase. Its actual load, tack, rider geometry, mounting/dismounting cost and ordinary independent temperament remain. One shared Bonus Action command and one offensive companion action per owner per numbered round apply where those source engines impose them. This feat supplies no blanket override of a specific engine’s attack or no-resource restrictions.

NEW ACQ-05 purchase/bond distinction: acquire Animal Companion once by committing one actual earned unspent feat opportunity while meeting its actual Animal Handling proficiency prerequisite and all other acquisition gates. Record that paid grant and its acquisition snapshot atomically. The animal and bonding hour are not conditions of purchasing the feat. Ownership begins at that commitment, with no companion and one unspent bond attempt under FS-06; it grants neither an animal nor an earlier completed Long Rest. Animal identity, matching template and any actually sourced sense choice belong to each bond record, not a permanently locked feat-purchase choice. The retained nonrepeatability/permanent-choice metadata does not prohibit the replacements expressly allowed here. Canceling a proposed purchase before commitment spends no opportunity. A completed purchase is not refunded or repeated because no animal is available, a bond attempt fails, or a bond later ends. Animal Companion ownership alone can satisfy Companion Training's printed parent alternative, but supplies neither its separate feat opportunity nor a creature on which to use it.

NEW ACQ-05 bond attempt: an owner of this feat with actual Animal Handling proficiency, no current feat bond, no other pending bond attempt, an unspent attempt and any required post-bond-ending Long Rest may select one already real, positive-HP living, willing/tamed, noncorrupted Beast with INT<7 fitting one of the three finite templates. The selected animal must have no incompatible existing bond, including another Animal Companion or Ranger bond. Finding, buying or taming it still needs actual lawful access and its real willing/tamed relationship to this owner; no animal, stocked shop, consent or charm is supplied. Preserve its actual identity, ordinary profile, current/maximum HP, conditions, injuries, native movement, breathing, custody and required template choices. In one ordered start event, recheck admission, reserve this owner and animal for the work, spend the one attempt, and begin the hour. Merely proposing a target or rejecting it before that event does not spend an attempt; it never reverses a previously completed feat purchase. Starting costs no RP, second feat opportunity or universal fee. An attempt cannot begin while an existing feat bond is retained; such a rejected proposal does not release or alter that bond.

Spend one uninterrupted hour of actual bonding work together at touch range. Keep the same owner and animal, actual access, the required proficiency and animal eligibility throughout the work and at completion; the owner must remain able to perform it. This is active work, not beneficial rest, and grants no extra work Watch, assistant shortcut, handover or overlapping incompatible task. Loss of required touch-range access, willing/tamed eligibility, qualifying body state, or the owner's ability to continue, including incapacitation, or voluntary abandonment terminates the attempt. Elapsed time, real losses and the spent attempt persist; no partial hour, resumed fraction or same-epoch retry is awarded. The prospective animal remains in its actual current ordinary state; no feat profile or command entitlement was installed. After a full lawful hour, atomically complete the one bond and apply the existing template/HP conversion to the animal's latest lawful ordinary state, using the owner's then-current governing statistics. No new bond check or success chance is added. Admission alone or an incomplete hour cannot establish a companion.

The initial allowance is one attempt at feat purchase. Each genuinely completed beneficial owner Long Rest thereafter sets the allowance to one, never adds a stored second attempt. Apply FS-06's actual rest limits and one elapsed clock: no reset from Short Rest, debt-only Rest, a repeated rest receipt, a scene, a new target, a new controller, a new day label or level growth. Do not credit active bonding or release work as rest. An invalid claimed completion record is evidence rejection, not an attempt or feat-payment refund: reconcile the real start/interruption/rest history. Missing history cannot be replaced by an assumed unspent allowance. One feat bond at a time. Use the template corresponding to the real animal's body/native movement; do not turn a dog into a bird or grant a new breathing mode. AC12+floor(ownerPB/2), maximumHP5+total owner level; template attack/ability/movement values are explicit NEW. At initial bond convert existing HP proportionally max(1,floor(newMax×oldHP/oldMax)); preserve actual conditions/injuries. Later maximum growth never heals, decreases clamp without damage. Ordinary legal healing works, but no Hit Dice/rest-refill is invented. Use one shared BA command within60ft while the animal can perceive you: in its attached phase after your regular turn, move and make its one attack or Dash/Disengage/Help/Dodge. No independent turn/Reaction; uncommanded move defensively and Dodge. The animal's HP-only chassis dies at0, producing its one actual corpse and ending the bond, with no Wound/death-save sequence; this is a feat-specific NEW rule, not generic animal law. NEW ACQ-05 replacement boundary: when an established feat bond ends through release or death, record that actual ending event. Before this owner begins any later feat bond, require a genuinely beneficial owner Long Rest whose completion is ordered after that event, as well as an available attempt, a real eligible living target and the full new hour. A rest completed before the ending event or an unused prior allowance cannot satisfy that replacement gate. A qualifying completion after the event is sufficient; no additional rule requires the whole rest to have started after it. Existing active-work/rest restrictions still apply. Replacement is a use of the already-owned nonrepeatable feat, not a second purchase. NEW explicit rebond interpretation: a previously released living animal may be selected again if it genuinely qualifies; it is a new bond to the same physical individual, not a new or refreshed animal. A dead animal never becomes eligible merely through rest, release, purchase or this procedure. Voluntary release requires the owner's one uninterrupted hour of actual release work. NEW ACQ-05 release boundary: record its start, but end the bond only on lawful completion; interruption or abandonment grants no partial-hour credit and leaves the existing bond intact unless an independent event already ended it. A fresh release hour may be begun while the bond still exists. Release consumes no bond attempt, feat opportunity or RP. It does not require a second target or borrow the bonding hour's touch-range requirement; actual owner capacity and uninterrupted work remain mandatory. At completion restore the same living animal's saved ordinary profile with the existing positive-current-HP ratio conversion, preserving its current conditions, injuries and actual custody without healing or refilling it. End the outgoing bond's control entitlement and unexecuted commands; preserve all already-spent body/actor allowances. No automatic transfer of custody or command occurs. Record this end for the post-ending Long-Rest gate. A creature cannot simultaneously have this and a Ranger bond, or two owners' Animal Companion bonds. NEW ACQ-05 correction of 'new paid acquisition': a transfer requires the outgoing bond to end through its actual lawful release/death/termination procedure, real lawful access/custody for the receiver, and the receiver's independently authorized new bond. An existing Animal Companion feat owner does not buy that nonrepeatable feat again; they spend their own available attempt and full hour and satisfy their own post-ending Long-Rest gate, if any. The sender's rest, feat ownership or spent attempt neither transfers nor resets the receiver's history. A receiver without this feat must first acquire it through their own actual eligible unspent opportunity, or use an independently acquired receiving engine; receiving the animal grants no feat or class feature. An actual Ranger Beast Companion route retains its own acquired Warder/class-level/selection gates, eligible-beast limits, 4 RP, one-hour touch procedure, once-per-beneficial-owner-Long-Rest allowance and native profile/lifecycle. This feat's no-RP route, release hour and attempt rules do not waive or redefine that class engine. A Ranger bond cannot be ended by invoking another engine's feat-release permission. No universal transfer payment, new animal, healing, additive chassis, second controller, extra phase or refunded body/resource budget is granted. Owner death ends the bond and, if the animal remains alive, restores its saved ordinary profile using the same positive-HP ratio conversion as release; a dead animal remains its actual corpse. Temporary owner incapacity prevents new commands but does not cancel a previously committed legal command; after that command, uncommanded phases remain defensive. This never supplies autonomous attacks.
NEW explicit EX58 interface: retain one real creature identity and one current control/phase record. Riding, bonding or transferring custody does not clone a turn, movement budget, Reaction, attack allowance, body or resource pool. An attached companion acts in its source-defined phase after the owner’s regular turn; a controlled mount uses EX58’s actual mounted-phase procedure. A body fitting both roles elects one compatible route before that round’s work, preserves all already-spent allowances and cannot switch routes to gain a second phase. Its actual load, tack, rider geometry, mounting/dismounting cost and ordinary independent temperament remain. One shared Bonus Action command and one offensive companion action per owner per numbered round apply where those source engines impose them. This feat supplies no blanket override of a specific engine’s attack or no-resource restrictions.
The three supplied body templates are NEW complete feat chassis, not evidence that such a Beast is available. Use only the corresponding real body/native mode. Saved ordinary maximum/currentHP and original constituent identity are required before bonding; no missing oldHP record is replaced by invented full health. The feat’s0HP-death rule applies only to this feat chassis; an independently governed mount/Ranger chassis retains its own rules rather than taking both.

mandatorySelectionsAndSnapshots.exactObligation: No permanent animal/template selection at feat purchase. Each later admitted bond records real individual, matching SUP-02 body and any actually sourced sense; replacements retain same feat ownership.

initialState.exactObligation: At paid feat commitment: owned=true, one unspent bond attempt, no bond/animal/profile conversion and no invented LR. Attempt spent at valid start, not completion.
initialState.laterEventsNotAcquisition: ACQ05 full uninterrupted hour, latest ordinary HP ratio, release/death and receiver-native transfer rules remain. Old completion-first model is historical, not current purchase evidence.

conditionalOrDeferred.boundary: All actual printed/operative qualifications remain required. Literal legacy lineage/Spellcraft/context branches remain conditional unless their exact source is present; current actual alternatives are retained. currentPublic.name: Appraise

sourceObject.name: Appraise
sourceObject.description: You can accurately determine the value of items.
sourceObject.effect: You can determine the exact value and properties of any item with a successful Investigation check.

currentPublic.operationalRules:
Spend ten active minutes closely inspecting one actual item with adequate sensory access and tools appropriate to safely examine it. NEW: make Intelligence (Investigation), DC10 for a plainly identifiable mundane object,15 for complex mundane construction,20 for an ordinary magical item, or25 for a unique unfamiliar construction; a specific item's explicit identification DC or concealment exception controls instead. Set the classification and actual information before rolling. On Success or Critical Success, learn its exact current reference value and complete discoverable operative properties, including magical properties and a curse unless that curse's specific source prevents this identification. Reference value means the recorded undamaged catalog price adjusted by the governing condition/valuation rule, or a Director-established local fair-market valuation when no catalog price exists, fixed before the roll. It is not a guaranteed purchase or sale offer. The property result states uses, limits, charges, activation and known operational risks from the actual item's complete record; it does not invent a missing profile, formula, historical truth or cosmology. A source explicitly resisting identification may withhold its protected part while other properties are identified. Safe appraisal is not activation or disarming; actual independent touch/proximity triggers remain. Failure spends time and yields no exact appraisal; another attempt needs changed evidence, access or method. This explicitly adopts the powerful source item-identification benefit. It differs from the reviewed Identify procedure; it does not amend Identify or make its protected disclosures public.
NEW settlement binding: a Haven Appraisal remains the full thirty-minute EX58 procedure with its own governing DC, actor, evidence and one check. This ten-minute direct examination may be performed as a genuine included part of that same appraisal, not as a free second valuation, skipped twenty minutes or concurrent second job. Standalone appraisal does not itself execute title/provenance, buyer negotiation, tax, sponsor, insurance or settlement. Reference price, actual agreed gross price and net receipts remain separate; apply FS-13 and the retained greater-of assay rule.
workedCases: A known item with reference value40gp can be appraised at40gp while a real buyer offers only20gp. The feat identifies the reference value; it does not compel that buyer to pay40gp.

An ordinary magical wand's complete operative profile can be learned on the proposed DC20 success. An explicitly identification-proof curse remains protected by its own source; its lore is not invented.

sourceObject.name: Arcane Flexibility
sourceObject.description: Careful preparation leaves room to exchange one readied spell when the party rests.
sourceObject.effect: When you finish a short rest, exchange one prepared spell for another spell of the same tier that your class can prepare.
sourceObject.legacyEffect: Swap one prepared spell per rest
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: At completion of each beneficial Short Rest, optionally replace exactly one currently prepared spell in one actual class preparation list with another spell of the same rank in that same class. It must already be a legal known/book/repertoire choice under that class’s preparation procedure and current class level/school limits. Decide after ordinary rest endpoints/recovery; record the previous and replacement preparation. No extra prepared capacity, learned spell, copied grant or class alias. A class without a preparation list gains no new list. NEW unpreparing does not retroactively dispel a legally ongoing spell; maintain its actual concentration/deadline, but no new cast through the removed preparation. One exchange per rest event across classes, not one per class or duplicate feat representation.

currentPublic.name: Arcane Focus

sourceObject.name: Arcane Focus
sourceObject.description: You can focus magical energy more effectively.
sourceObject.effect: You can use your spellcasting focus to cast spells without material components worth less than 100 gp.

currentPublic.operationalRules: When you personally cast a spell you are actually entitled to cast, you may use a complete functional focus legal for that casting source to replace material-component requirements whose specified reference value is strictly less than100gp. NEW: this is an explicit exception for both consumed and nonconsumed components; total repeated units of the same required component within this cast before comparing the threshold. Components without an explicit price qualify as ordinary unpriced materials; a source-specific unique named object, target/body or expressly irreplaceable component does not become an unpriced generic material. A100gp component does not qualify. Hold/manipulate or display the focus exactly as the governing source permits; S,V,casting time,RP,concentration and other requirements remain. This feat cannot replace the actual target, a creature’s remains as a target, an item being enchanted or a required personally bonded object. For a reviewed Scribing payload actually cast by you, use the same cast-level rule only if otherwise eligible; activating a noncast magic item does not invoke this feat. Crafting ingredients, sacrificial recipe bodies, research costs and stored spell creation remain real unless their own exact procedure is a qualifying cast. Record each waived component and its stated reference value; market discounts cannot push an intrinsically100gp component under the threshold.

sourceObject.description: Condensed force erupts around the caster, driving nearby foes away from the blast.
sourceObject.effect: As an action, spend 3 RP to release force in a 10-foot radius. Creatures of your choice make a Strength save against your spell save DC, taking 3d6 force damage and being pushed 10 feet on a failure, or half damage without the push on a success.

NEW this is a magical feat technique, not an ordinary spell: no rank, spell components, Counterspell window or Dissonance/Refrain from this activation. Center a 10 ft radius on your own occupied space under ordinary area geometry. Choose perceived creatures with line of effect in it, including yourself if desired, before rolling. Roll 3d6 force once. Each makesSTRsave: failure full damage then push up to 10 ft directly away from the origin along a legal unobstructed route; success half damage rounded down, no push. Self can take damage but has no away-from-self push. Stop at obstruction/occupied destination; no collision damage, opportunity attack or unstated prone. Large bodies retain real fitting requirements. Immunity to forced movement blocks only push.

currentPublic.name: Athlete

sourceObject.name: Athlete
sourceObject.description: You have undergone extensive physical training to gain the following benefits:
sourceObject.effect: Increase Strength or Dexterity by 1, climbing doesn't cost extra movement, running long jump distance increases by feet equal to Strength modifier

currentPublic.operationalRules: Choose Strength or Dexterity and increase it by 1, normally no higher than 20. Climbing does not cost extra movement solely because it is climbing; terrain, crawling, squeezing and other independent costs remain. This grants no climbing Speed, handholds, ceiling adhesion, automatic check success or immunity to falls. For a running long jump, add your current Strength modifier in feet to the otherwise legal horizontal distance. NEW: the increase has a minimum of zero when that modifier is negative, and a running approach requires at least 10 feet of actual immediately preceding movement on support. The approach and jump both spend movement; clearance, checks and legal landing remain. This does not increase a high jump or ordinary standing long jump. Improved Athlete's separate proposal supplies its own standing-distance change and retains this running increase once. The approach and negative-modifier completions require the full movement-source decision before adoption.
workedCases: A legal running jump with baseline 16 feet and STR modifier +3 can span 19 feet, still paid from actual movement after its approach.
A character with STR modifier -1 gains no extra jump distance and suffers no extra one-foot reduction from this feat. Difficult terrain on a climb still costs its terrain surcharge.

currentPublic.name: Battle Awareness

sourceObject.name: Battle Awareness
sourceObject.description: A combatant reads pressure at the flank and shifts clear before an opening becomes a strike.
sourceObject.effect: Enemies do not gain advantage merely for flanking you, and you gain +1 AC against opportunity attacks.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: At total level5, opponents receive no attack advantage against you merely because they flank you. Current reviewed combat supplies no universal flanking advantage, and the proposed Tactical Flanker geometry grants only its explicit damage rider; this protection creates no penalty for other defenders and does not erase that separate damage rider. Any independently sourced flanking-advantage rule is suppressed only as an advantage source against you; other advantage still works and ordinary cancellation applies. Gain+1AC only against an actual opportunity attack while that one attack resolves, including a legal feat-specific entry opportunity attack. No lasting AC, immunity or protection from a Reaction attack that is not actually an opportunity attack.
workedCases: A normal attack from a flanking foe has no new benefit to remove; Tactical Flanker's lawful1d6 remains separate.
An entry-trigger polearm opportunity attack compares against+1AC. Mage Slayer's non-opportunity Reaction attack does not.

currentPublic.name: Battle Mage

sourceObject.name: Battle Mage
sourceObject.description: You blend magic and martial combat.
sourceObject.prerequisite: Spellcasting ability, proficiency with martial weapons
sourceObject.effect: You can cast spells with somatic components while holding weapons and shields.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Require actual personal spellcasting and a genuine martial-weapon proficiency grant; NEW one specified martial weapon proficiency is sufficient, without inventing proficiency with all martial weapons. For a spell you personally cast, one hand otherwise legally holding a weapon or shield may perform that spell’s S gestures while retaining that object. The hand and limb must still be capable of the required motion; restraints, missing anatomy or a feature explicitly forbidding gestures are not bypassed. NEW a buckler-occupied hand can use this same narrow S exception despite its ordinary lack of a free S hand. This gives no extra hands for loading, material manipulation, grappling, tools or wielding. A two-handed weapon can be held through the gestures, but its actual attack still requires its normal grip. F must independently be supplied by a legal focus; holding a sword does not make it a focus. V, priced/consumed materials, actual source access and nonproficient armor casting/concentration consequences remain. No advantage on concentration or Reaction spell is granted by this feat.
workedCases: A caster with an actual martial sword proficiency holds sword and shield and can supply S through one hand under this feat. A spell also requiring F still needs an independently legal focus arrangement.
Binding both hands so gestures cannot be made still prevents S. The feat does not remove a nonproficient armor RP surcharge or concentration disadvantage.

currentPublic.name: Battle Ready

sourceObject.name: Battle Ready
sourceObject.description: You are always prepared for combat.
sourceObject.effect: You can don or doff armor in half the normal time and have advantage on initiative rolls.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Don or doff an actual suit of armor in half its normal time, preserving its real steps, access, hands, closures and fit. NEW: apply this factor once to the selected suit's existing armor duration; do not automatically include shields, weapons, jewelry or other gear. Combine the separately authorized single helper's doff-time halving multiplicatively with this feat because they represent distinct sources, then round elapsed time upward once to a whole second. In initiative, spend enough complete Actions/turn intervals to cover that elapsed work without compressing an Action below its legal availability; partial progress is retained only to the extent the armor procedure actually permits. Extra helpers do not further halve the time. Interruption leaves the real partially completed state and does not make the armor usable sooner. Gain advantage on each actual initiative roll; this creates neither a new roll after order is established nor an extra turn. Multiple initiative-advantage sources do not stack.
workedCases: A normal 60-second armor doff becomes 30 seconds; one real helper can reduce it to 15 seconds under this proposed composition. Two helpers do not reduce it to 7.5 seconds.
A shield whose separate rule takes one Action still takes that Action; the feat does not convert it to a free interaction.

currentPublic.name: Battlefield Commander

sourceObject.name: Battlefield Commander
sourceObject.description: A commanding voice directs three nearby allies into more favorable positions when the line must shift.
sourceObject.effect: As an action, choose up to three willing allies within 30 feet who can hear you. Each may use its reaction to move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks. You regain this use after a short rest.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules:
Action, once per short rest: choose one to three willing allied creatures, including yourself, within30ft who can hear and understand the brief directive. Lock recipients and their order, spend the use, then resolve each sequentially. Each may spend its own available Reaction immediately for a separate floor(current relevant Speed/2)-ft movement-cost budget. Recheck hearing, willingness, position and capability at that recipient's resolution. Terrain and hazards apply; movement from this instruction provokes no opportunity attacks. Speed0 gives no movement. Declining or losing eligibility grants no replacement recipient and does not refund the commander; a recipient that does not move need not spend a Reaction. No ordinary movement/Action/BA resource is restored.
SOURCE SCOPE CORRECTION: “allies” includes the feat owner unless the actual clause says “other.” The owner must still meet the same hearing/perception, range, willing-target and action/resource predicates. No second body, observer or extra action is created by self-eligibility. This sentence supersedes any narrower owner-exclusion in the submitted proposal, not the preserved original.
workedCases: The commander selects themselves and two willing hearing allies, spends the Action and short-rest use, then resolves their chosen order. Each moving recipient pays their own Reaction for half-current-Speed movement; the commander has no extra Reaction.
The second ally is incapacitated by a hazard while the first moves: skip that ally; the third may still react if legal.

currentPublic.name: Battlefield Tactician

sourceObject.name: Battlefield Tactician
sourceObject.description: Soldierly analysis lends a practiced edge to every tactics roll.
sourceObject.effect: +2 bonus to tactics rolls.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: NEW: Soldier means at least one actually acquired level in the Soldier Base class; a background title, uniform, rank or NPC occupation alone does not satisfy it. Add +2 when the Director calls for an ability check whose declared goal is evaluating a concrete battlefield plan, deployment, approach, withdrawal or fortification. Intelligence (Investigation) analyzes visible formations and routes; Intelligence (History) recalls an actually studied battle or doctrine; Intelligence (Engineering) evaluates a constructed defense. Use another ability/skill only when the actual task warrants it, with PB once. Do not roll merely to obtain the bonus. The result supplies the ordinary task's actionable information or plan, not extra allied attacks, higher class save DCs, free Overwatch, advance knowledge of hidden forces or compelled obedience. Timing and information access belong to that actual planning task.
workedCases: A Soldier 1 with INT 14 and Investigation proficiency analyzes an observed barricade: d20 + INT + PB + 2. Their later crossbow attack receives none of the tactics bonus.
A character with a soldier-themed background but zero Soldier class levels does not meet this proposed acquisition gate.

currentPublic.name: Beast Whisperer

sourceObject.name: Beast Whisperer
sourceObject.description: Steady rapport with animals keeps a handling attempt from becoming a critical failure.
sourceObject.effect: When you roll a natural 1 on an Animal Handling check, treat the die as a 2. You can communicate simple emotional intent to beasts through posture and sound.
sourceObject.legacyEffect: Handle animal checks never fail critically
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: On an actual Animal Handling check, replace every d20 face of 1 with an effective face of 2 before selecting the advantage/disadvantage die, calculating the total and applying fixed-DC natural shifts. Keep the rolled face in history, but use 2 for this check's natural-result rule. Apply the same replacement to any lawfully rerolled die. It is a replacement, not another roll or a reroll trigger. A margin can still produce Critical Failure; the broader legacy promise is not adopted. Through observable posture and audible sound, communicate a simple emotional intent such as calm, warning, approach or leave. The beast must perceive the relevant signal. This grants neither language comprehension nor obedience, a trained mount, communication through total sensory obstruction, nor a changed attitude. A check is required only where the ordinary interaction calls for one.
workedCases: At DC 20 with modifier +2, a raw 1 becomes effective 2, total 4. The result remains Critical Failure by margin, without a further natural-1 downgrade.
Disadvantage faces 1/17 become 2/17; select 2. A deaf beast that sees a calming posture may perceive that signal, but it receives no spoken instructions it cannot understand.

currentPublic.name: Berserker

sourceObject.name: Berserker
sourceObject.description: You can enter a battle rage.
sourceObject.effect: Once per long rest, you can rage for 1 minute, gaining +2 damage on melee attacks and resistance to physical damage.

currentPublic.operationalRules: NEW: as a Bonus Action, spend the feat's one long-rest use to enter this feat rage for one elapsed minute. Gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage, whether magical or nonmagical, and add 2 damage on each actual successful melee attack you own. The melee scope includes weapon, unarmed, natural and melee spell attacks; it is not limited to weapons. Add the flat 2 once to the attack's primary damage type before target defenses; it is not doubled by a critical hit and is not a separate hit, copied damage or spellcasting trigger. NEW: the rage ends early if you voluntarily end it as a Bonus Action or become Incapacitated. It does not require attacking or taking damage to continue, prohibit spellcasting/concentration, extend through repeated attacks, or grant unstated class rage features. Another real rage may coexist under its own rules, but same-scope resistance does not stack and bonuses obey their actual families; this feat's flat rider cannot be counted twice under aliases. A completed rest restores the use, not an encounter declaration.
workedCases: A critical melee weapon hit doubles its actual damage dice but adds this feat's flat 2 only once. A separate ranged attack receives none of this rider.
An already bludgeoning-resistant holder remains resistant, not quarter-damage, when the rage begins. Becoming Stunned ends this proposed rage through Incapacitated.

sourceObject.description: A precise melee critical opens a wound that carries the feat's listed bleed effect.
sourceObject.effect: When you score a critical hit with a melee weapon, the target bleeds for 1d4 damage at the start of each of its turns for 3 rounds. A creature can use an action to stop the bleeding with a successful Medicine check against DC 10 + your proficiency bonus.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

Same-owner reapplication refreshes three remaining ticks without adding a second instance; different owners retain competing groups under the existing highest-expected-damage/earliest-application arbitration. Losing due groups still spend ticks. Snapshot the ending Medicine DC10+your PB at application. currentPublic.name: Blind Fight

sourceObject.name: Blind Fight
sourceObject.description: You can fight without relying on sight.
sourceObject.effect: You don't suffer disadvantage on attack rolls due to being blinded, and you can pinpoint the location of creatures within 30 feet.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Ignore only attack disadvantage directly imposed by your Blinded condition. Other independent unseen-target, darkness, long-range or condition disadvantages remain. NEW pinpointing is a nonvisual spatial sense: while conscious, automatically know the occupied location of an actual creature within30ft with line of effect, unless it is behind total cover or protected by an explicit anti-detection effect. It needs no hearing or sight and so works while Deafened/Blinded; those bodily consequences otherwise remain. This specific sense defeats a Hidden location within range for you but does not supply visual sight, colors, text, identity/type or perceive objects as creatures. An invisible creature's located position follows the current Invisible known-position exception; separate darkness can still impose unseen penalties. A creature you can see spell still needs actual qualifying sight, not this pinpoint. Leaving range loses live localization; remembered last position is not a new exact current one.

A creature behind a closed solid wall is not pinpointed, even within10ft; known location outside30 does not remain automatically tracked.

currentPublic.name: Blind Fighting

sourceObject.name: Blind Fighting
sourceObject.description: You can fight effectively without sight.
sourceObject.effect: You have blindsight with a range of 10 feet. You can effectively see anything within this range that isn't behind total cover.

currentPublic.operationalRules: NEW interpret the literal10ft effectively-see clause as a nonvisual blindsight sense while conscious. Within10ft and line of effect, you can effectively see actual creatures/objects regardless of ordinary darkness, fog, Blinded or invisibility; total cover and explicit blindsight/anti-detection blockers still prevent it. Hearing is not required. It meets an ordinary can-see targeting requirement within that range but cannot read colors, printed text or visual illusion details that require actual eyes; it perceives physical shapes/presence, not a secret true identity or magical aura. Hidden creatures with an exposed physical body in this range are seen by you and therefore not Hidden from you. A purely visual illusion without a physical body is not a real body to this sense; this does not grant other observers automatic disbelief. Beyond10ft use normal senses. Blind Fight's30ft pinpoint range does not extend this10ft effective sight.
workedCases: A creature5ft away in opaque fog can be effectively seen for a can-see spell if line of effect remains.
Owning both feats locates an enemy20ft away but does not extend blindsight or can-see permission to20ft.

sourceObject.name: Blood Magic
sourceObject.description: An experienced caster draws on their own vitality to boost a spell.
sourceObject.effect: When casting a spell, you may take necrotic damage equal to twice the spell tier to increase its save DC by 1 or add one damage die. This damage cannot be reduced. Once used, you cannot use this feat again until a short rest.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Once per beneficial SR or LR, when committing an actual spell, declare either+1 to that cast’s spell-save DC or one extra native damage die under the shared added-die procedure. Pay the spell’s actual ordinary costs plus 2×its actual rank as the shared unreducible-necrotic normal HP cost, before establishing its new concentration and opening interruption. Existing concentration must face the self-damage normally before displacement; death/action loss aborts the unfinished spell without refund. Rank 0 explicitly costs 0 HP but still spends the feat use; a cantrip is not excluded by the source. DC mode changes all actual saves caused by that same cast, including its legal repeats, while that cast lasts; it supplies no saves to automatic effects and no inherited DC for unrelated children. Damage mode cannot modify a flat-only or nondamaging spell. No two modes, doubled cast orHPrefund; copying never regrants the modifier.
workedCases: Rank 2 spell DC 14 becomes 15 after 4 normal HP cost; an ordinary area save for each target uses 15.

Preserve its actual advantage/disadvantage configuration, rolling the appropriate new d20 set, not choosing freely among old and new dice. No Action/Reaction is required. Off-turn saves and extra turns grant no entitlement, even if the standalone source says per turn. No banking. Applicable other reroll features retain their real limits; choose a legal order, never revisit a consumed stage.

sourceObject.name: Brace for Impact
sourceObject.description: A resilient combatant who holds position braces for the listed damage resistance.
sourceObject.effect: If you have not moved since the start of your turn, use a reaction when you take damage to reduce it by your proficiency bonus + Constitution modifier.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: If you have undergone no actual positional displacement since your most recent original regular-turn start, spend Reaction when a direct damage event would damage you. NEW all voluntary, forced, carried and teleport displacement counts, even returning to the same square; standing, turning in place and a failed move do not. Before your first encounter turn, count displacement since encounter entry. Reduce one whole resolved incoming event by max(0,PB+CON modifier), after ordinary passive defenses and before temporary HP. Allocate reduction across components in their stable order, never below0; one attack's fire and slashing are one event, separate attacks are not. Do not re-mitigate a transferred packet that explicitly forbids recipient mitigation. This affects damage only, not attached conditions, sacrificed HP or state assignment. Paying with a zero reduction is allowed but does not create healing.

currentPublic.name: Break Line

sourceObject.name: Break Line
sourceObject.description: An agile veteran slips through the enemy's frontline zone without treating it as an obstacle.
sourceObject.effect: Once per turn, you may move through the space of one hostile creature no more than one size larger than you. That creature may make an opportunity attack; on a miss, you complete the movement.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Once per turn during your own legal voluntary movement, declare crossing one hostile creature's occupied space whose size is no more than one category larger. You must have enough ordinary remaining movement cost and a visible or known legal unoccupied exit to traverse its entire occupied footprint; occupied terrain costs at least difficult. Before first entry, that creature may spend its Reaction for one legal melee opportunity attack against you, even though you are entering rather than leaving. All actual reaction, sight, reach and opportunity-immunity restrictions apply. If it hits, this passage fails: remain in your last legal outside space, spend the first attempted entry step's cost and the feat use. The hit's other consequences resolve normally. If it misses, declines, cannot attack or its opportunity attack is suppressed, proceed, paying actual traversal costs. Recheck the exit after interruptions; if traversal becomes impossible before entry, stay outside and spend the committed use. Do not willingly start a traversal without a complete legal route. Other creatures may make normal opportunity attacks. This does not shove or phase through a creature.
workedCases: A Medium rogue has20 movement cost left and crosses one Medium hostile square for10 then exits for5. The guard has no Reaction, so passage succeeds.
The guard's legal special attack hits. The rogue remains before the occupied square and spends10 cost for the attempted difficult entry; damage and the once-turn use remain.

currentPublic.name: Burglar

sourceObject.name: Burglar
sourceObject.description: You are skilled at breaking and entering.
sourceObject.effect: You gain proficiency with thieves' tools and can pick locks and disable traps more effectively.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Gain thieves’-tools proficiency. NEW completion of “more effectively”: add+2 to actual checks using those tools to pick an accessible mechanical lock or safely disable an identified, accessible mechanical trap. PB still applies once; tool expertise replaces PB rather than adding another PB. This benefit does not reveal traps, find secret passages, open a structure without manipulating its lock or disarm an effect that has no usable mechanical disarm interface. Use the actual lock/trap’s printed time, DC, failure and retry procedure; for the reviewed ordinary mechanical lock, retain one Action and DC15, with failure consuming time and an unchanged-state retry requiring a materially different supported approach, better tools or new evidence. Simple obvious unlocked mechanisms need no roll. Magical devices keep explicit magical disarm requirements; a genuine mechanical safety on one can be manipulated only within its actual scope. This feat grants no trap immunity or faster-than-source Action. A different lock or trap without a governing profile requires its actual bounded mechanism/time/DC, not an automatic ordinary-lock conversion.

sourceObject.description: Your cantrips become more powerful.
sourceObject.effect: Choose one cantrip you know. It deals maximum damage when you roll a natural 20 on the attack roll or the target rolls a natural 1 on their saving throw.

currentPublic.operationalRules:

When your actual attack for that chosen rank0spell keeps a natural20, maximize that attack’s eligible direct spell damage dice after its normal critical dice doubling. When an actual target’s saving throw against a particular damage event of that cantrip keeps a natural1, maximize that target’s eligible damage dice for that event. NEW a saved natural1 remains a successful save if its actual total meets DC: this trigger does not turn success into failure or create damage where the card gives none; if success gives half damage, halve the maximized lawful amount normally.

Maximize the chosen spell’s own dice plus dice explicitly added to that spell’s damage roll, not independent weapon, class/feat or item damage riders. Keep flat bonuses unchanged. Resolve each actual attack/save event separately; a natural20on one ray does not maximize a different ray, all area targets or later ongoing damage. A target-specific natural1on a shared area save uses the maximum native-dice value for that target only; other targets retain the ordinary shared rolled value. A later genuine damage-triggering save can qualify independently, but an earlier failed save supplies no permanent maximum-damage state. A no-roll automatic hit/failure or critical-range19is not a natural20/1. NEW a would-be damage die replaced with its maximum is not actually rolled for Evocation Focus; do not roll meaningless dice merely to obtain that other feat’s bonus. No ordinary cantrip scaling is added.

currentPublic.name: Cartographer

sourceObject.name: Cartographer
sourceObject.description: You excel at navigation and mapmaking.
sourceObject.effect: You can create accurate maps and never get lost. You have advantage on Survival checks for navigation.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Create an accurate record of a route or place you actually observe, using real recording materials. NEW: record one minute of active map work for each distinct junction or approximately100feet of visible route, whichever requires more work; a scale overview from a clear vantage can be recorded in ten minutes. Ordinary mapping is separate work unless another feature, such as Dungeon Cartographer, permits concurrent normal-pace mapping. 'Never get lost' means you retain a reliable account of your own traversed path and current position relative to its still-valid recorded landmarks: you cannot accidentally choose a wrong already-known branch solely through a navigation failure. It does not reveal an unvisited area, locate an unknown destination, connect an unobserved teleportation gap or preserve a physically destroyed route. A changed or illusory landmark may require investigation; the feat preserves what was actually perceived rather than certifying it true. Gain advantage on actual Survival navigation checks, including where incomplete new information still makes the route uncertain. Others using your map receive its actual information, not your personal never-lost guarantee or advantage unless another feature grants it.
workedCases: On an unchanged route the holder already traversed, a failed navigation check cannot make them accidentally take the wrong recorded junction. A missing bridge still requires a real solution.
After an unobserved teleportation, the old map remains accurate where its terrain survives, but the feat supplies no invented connection between departure and arrival.

While legally riding a real mount under actual mounted/control/custody rules, your attacks have advantage against actual unmounted creatures. Retain the broad source: melee/ranged weapon, unarmed/natural and spell attacks qualify, with no target-size restriction. Save-only effects do not. Other disadvantage still cancels. The ridden mount's existing Speed modes each gain10ft while you remain its actual rider; NEW derive any mode explicitly equal to another Speed from that modified value rather than adding10 twice. No new mode is created, and Speed0 restrictions override the increase. Multiple Cavalry riders give one+10 family bonus, not one per passenger. The feat creates no mount, control permission, mount attack, shared Action pool or extra turn. Mounted Combatant remains a separate narrower feat with no double advantage. Exact mounting, load and shared-space procedures follow the completed EX58 transport verdict now, not a future placeholder.
NEW explicit EX58 interface: retain one real creature identity and one current control/phase record. Riding, bonding or transferring custody does not clone a turn, movement budget, Reaction, attack allowance, body or resource pool. An attached companion acts in its source-defined phase after the owner’s regular turn; a controlled mount uses EX58’s actual mounted-phase procedure. A body fitting both roles elects one compatible route before that round’s work, preserves all already-spent allowances and cannot switch routes to gain a second phase. Its actual load, tack, rider geometry, mounting/dismounting cost and ordinary independent temperament remain. One shared Bonus Action command and one offensive companion action per owner per numbered round apply where those source engines impose them. This feat supplies no blanket override of a specific engine’s attack or no-resource restrictions.
Apply the one+10 to each independently existing mount Speed before its normal encumbrance/systemic/strongest-slow stages. A derived Speed uses its parent once. It does not modify a vehicle’s unrelated printed route speed, grant a mode, change carrying capacity or count mount displacement as the rider’s self-powered movement for a different feat.
workedCases: A mounted archer attacks an unmounted giant: Cavalry advantage applies despite its size, subject to other disadvantage.
Two Cavalry passengers do not give a horse+20Speed; no flying Speed appears on a walking-only mount.

sourceObject.description: Sustained focus carries a channel spell beyond its usual duration.
sourceObject.effect: When a spell requires you to spend an action on later turns to maintain it, you may maintain it once as a bonus action instead. You regain this use after a short rest.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Once per beneficial SR or LR, on your own actual later turn, replace one Action explicitly required solely to maintain one of your already established spells with one Bonus Action. Declare and consume at that maintenance commitment. Preserve concentration, RP/material upkeep, targeting, existing pulse/command limits and the original spell deadline. It cannot shorten initial casting, Ready setup, a ritual, an attack granted by the spell, or an optional Action to issue a new damaging command unless that exact source identifies it as required maintenance. An Action that combines required maintenance with another benefit retains the combined printed payload but still supplies no second occurrence. One actual BA must be available; Incapacitated/other restrictions still apply. The source’s prior 50% duration wording remains an inactive alternative.

sourceObject.description: You can make devastating charge attacks.
sourceObject.effect: When you use the Dash action, you can make one melee weapon attack or shove as a bonus action.

No second BA.

sourceObject.name: Chef

sourceObject.effect: You can cook special food during a long rest that provides temporary hit points to your party.

unchangedReviewedRecord.acquisition: Actual class feat selection; source-specific prerequisite at acquisition
unchangedReviewedRecord.operationalRules:
## Chef — General; no prerequisite

During an actual long-rest attempt, use cook's utensils and spend one uninterrupted hour cooking. This is permitted light activity only when the normal long-rest procedure permits that hour; the feat does not enlarge the allowance. Designate one batch of1..current PB intended servings at cooking start. Only one batch may be designated per rest attempt and only one can gain potency per successful completed rest.

On successful cooking completion, consume one real standard ration or meal-equivalent ingredient per intended serving. Create exactly that many physical prepared-food items, each with its own identity. Their food exists immediately, but they gain no feat potency before the rest actually succeeds. If the rest fails, the ingredients remain spent and the food remains ordinary. An incomplete cooking hour creates no special food.

At successful long-rest completion, first resolve old rest-expiring effects and advance the rest epoch. Then snapshot the Chef's current PB and empower up to `min(physically prepared servings still present, current PB)` items. Each grants `2 × PB at batch finalization` temporary HP. A PB increase cannot manufacture more ingredients or servings; a decrease leaves excess prepared items ordinary.

A creature with a legal serving must spend one uninterrupted minute eating it. Completing a legal offer consumes the serving and the recipient's **Chef-family entitlement for its current completed-long-rest epoch**, even if an equal/stronger existing grant wins. This limit is shared across every Chef. The Chef's own rest does not reset another recipient's entitlement.

Potency ends at the earlier of24 elapsed hours from successful batch creation or the Chef's next completed long rest after the creation rest. An already consumed/discarded item never returns. Expired potency leaves ordinary food, with no magical premium value. Potency expiration does not end a previously granted shield; that shield has the recipient's default lifetime.

Chef servings are distinct from crafted Feast recipes. Chef grants no recipe ingredients, crafting checks, RP restoration, creature traits or recipe power. It does not occupy the recipe system's one-feast-at-a-time slot. A lawful recipe rider can coexist with a Chef rider; temporary HP still do not stack. One physical meal cannot claim both effects unless an exact recipe expressly supports it. Recipe-specific ten-minute eating, longer crafting and materials remain independent.

**NEW:** the finite batch transaction, quantities, preparation/eating times, recipient-family cap, potency expiry and explicit no-duplication/economy bridges. The source's long-rest cooking role is preserved.

During an actual long-rest attempt, use cook's utensils and spend one uninterrupted hour cooking. This is permitted light activity only when the normal long-rest procedure permits that hour; the feat does not enlarge the allowance. Designate one batch of1..current PB intended servings at cooking start. Only one batch may be designated per rest attempt and only one can gain potency per successful completed rest.

On successful cooking completion, consume one real standard ration or meal-equivalent ingredient per intended serving. Create exactly that many physical prepared-food items, each with its own identity. Their food exists immediately, but they gain no feat potency before the rest actually succeeds. If the rest fails, the ingredients remain spent and the food remains ordinary. An incomplete cooking hour creates no special food.

At successful long-rest completion, first resolve old rest-expiring effects and advance the rest epoch. Then snapshot the Chef's current PB and empower up to `min(physically prepared servings still present, current PB)` items. Each grants `2 × PB at batch finalization` temporary HP. A PB increase cannot manufacture more ingredients or servings; a decrease leaves excess prepared items ordinary.

A creature with a legal serving must spend one uninterrupted minute eating it. Completing a legal offer consumes the serving and the recipient's **Chef-family entitlement for its current completed-long-rest epoch**, even if an equal/stronger existing grant wins. This limit is shared across every Chef. The Chef's own rest does not reset another recipient's entitlement.

Potency ends at the earlier of24 elapsed hours from successful batch creation or the Chef's next completed long rest after the creation rest. An already consumed/discarded item never returns. Expired potency leaves ordinary food, with no magical premium value. Potency expiration does not end a previously granted shield; that shield has the recipient's default lifetime.

Chef servings are distinct from crafted Feast recipes. Chef grants no recipe ingredients, crafting checks, RP restoration, creature traits or recipe power. It does not occupy the recipe system's one-feast-at-a-time slot. A lawful recipe rider can coexist with a Chef rider; temporary HP still do not stack. One physical meal cannot claim both effects unless an exact recipe expressly supports it. Recipe-specific ten-minute eating, longer crafting and materials remain independent.

**NEW:** the finite batch transaction, quantities, preparation/eating times, recipient-family cap, potency expiry and explicit no-duplication/economy bridges. The source's long-rest cooking role is preserved.

currentPublic.name: Cleave

sourceObject.name: Cleave
sourceObject.description: Your attacks can strike multiple foes.
sourceObject.effect: When you reduce a creature to 0 hit points with a melee attack, you can make another attack against a different creature within reach.

currentPublic.operationalRules: NEW once on your own turn, after your direct melee attack reduces a meaningful hostile from positiveHP to0, you may make one immediate additional melee weapon, natural or unarmed attack against a different creature within the actual reach of the selected legal attack. It costs no separate Action/BA but is exactly one attack, not Attack Action/Extra Attack. No melee spell may be cast through this grant. Death is unnecessary; an actually prevented drop gives no trigger. A different second target need not be hostile, but no staged friendly drop can generate the first trigger. Use current weapon/hands and normal attack/damage; no free draw. Mark the attack as derived under the shared causal cap so it cannot spawn Cleave, Frenzied Rage, Great Weapon Master or analogous further attack grants. If multiple extra-attack sources trigger on the same drop, NEW choose one grant for that event, pay its actual cost, and do not bank the others.
workedCases: A melee hit downs a hostile: make one immediate unarmed or weapon attack against another legal target.
That derived attack downs the next foe; it cannot spawn another Cleave or a Great Weapon Master entitlement.

sourceObject.name: Cleaving Momentum
sourceObject.description: A heavy two-handed finishing blow carries its momentum into the listed follow-up attack.
sourceObject.effect: When you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points with a melee weapon, make one melee weapon attack against another creature within reach as a bonus action.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Acquire with STR16 and actual proficiency in a Two-Handed weapon. NEW triggering and follow-up attacks must both use an actual melee weapon wielded with two hands; a legal Versatile two-hand attack can operate the acquired feat. During your own turn, after your attack reduces a genuine hostile creature from positiveHP to0 after floors/replacements, you may spend your still-available Bonus Action before that turn ends for one melee weapon attack against a different creature in legal reach. Death is unnecessary; a surviving downed opponent qualifies. The second target need not be hostile under the printed another-creature wording. Normal damage, ammunition if relevant, hands and perception apply. No banked off-turn use and no additional Bonus Action; multiple drops only provide alternative triggers for that same wallet. Copied/periodic damage and reducing an already0 creature do not qualify.
workedCases: A greatsword drops a hostile to0 but the creature survives dying. One available BA can attack a second target.
The follow-up also drops its target. There is no second Bonus Action and thus no chain of free attacks.

currentPublic.name: Climb Anywhere

sourceObject.name: Climb Anywhere
sourceObject.description: Practiced athletics removes the listed check penalty when scaling vertical surfaces.
sourceObject.effect: You gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed on surfaces with handholds. Climbing sheer or inverted surfaces still requires a check, but you do not suffer disadvantage solely because of the angle.
sourceObject.legacyEffect: No check penalty on vertical surfaces
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: While your current body has usable grasping anatomy and the surface has actual adequate handholds, gain a climbing Speed equal to your current legal walking Speed. Apply body, load, armor and condition limits that actually govern that movement; do not derive a fresh unpenalized speed. Expenditure still comes from the shared movement budget. A steep angle alone does not impose disadvantage on a required climbing check. A sheer or inverted route still needs a check and an actually supportable method: usable cracks, holds, rigging, an anchor or another explicit ability. This feat provides no adhesion to a smooth unsupported ceiling. The Director states grip failure, a fall or loss of progress before the check under the route's actual conditions. Other causes of disadvantage, required hands, hazardous surfaces and zero-Speed conditions remain.
workedCases: Walking Speed reduced from 30 to 20 gives climbing Speed 20 on a held wall. Moving 10 feet on the ground leaves 10 feet of this movement budget for climbing.

A perfectly smooth inverted ceiling with no anchor is not traversable solely with this feat. A rope-supported inverted traverse can be attempted, with no angle-only disadvantage but any actual slickness penalty intact.

sourceObject.name: Climber
sourceObject.description: You are an expert at scaling walls and cliffs.
sourceObject.effect: You gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed and advantage on Athletics checks made to climb.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Gain a climbing Speed equal to your current legal walking Speed and advantage on actual Athletics checks made to climb. NEW: derive the speed from the current body and applicable speed penalties, not an unmodified ancestral baseline. Follow the shared spent-movement-cost ledger when switching modes, so movement already spent is never refunded. Climbing still needs support your actual hands, limbs, equipment and surface can provide; the feat does not add adhesion, free hands or a flying mode. A check occurs only when the route calls for one, and advantage does not eliminate its real failure consequence. Grip, slippery material, load, damage, support collapse, zero Speed and falls keep their ordinary rules. A second feature granting the same climb Speed does not add another walking Speed; use the actual applicable movement profile.

currentPublic.name: Close Quarters Combat

sourceObject.name: Close Quarters Combat
sourceObject.description: Quick control of a cramped melee keeps a ranged attack from drawing the listed opportunity attack.
sourceObject.effect: Making a ranged attack while a hostile creature is within 5 feet does not impose disadvantage, and the attack does not provoke an opportunity attack.
sourceObject.legacyEffect: No AoO when using ranged in melee
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Your ranged attacks ignore disadvantage caused specifically by a seeing, non-Incapacitated hostile creature within5ft of you. This covers ranged weapon and ranged spell attacks. It does not remove long-range, unseen-target, Prone, restrained or other independent disadvantage. If any other disadvantage remains, apply ordinary cancellation. It is a fact about that exchange, not an ongoing mind-reading effect, a lie detector, an exact secret thought or proof of the speaker's factual claims.
