currentPublic.name: Commanding Presence

sourceObject.name: Commanding Presence
sourceObject.description: You naturally command respect.
sourceObject.effect: You can use your Charisma modifier instead of Strength for Intimidation checks, and you have advantage on Persuasion checks against creatures of lower level.

currentPublic.operationalRules: When an actual Intimidation task would use Strength, you may use Charisma instead; choose before rolling. Ordinary Charisma (Intimidation) already uses Charisma, so this clause gives no second modifier or bonus there. It does not grant proficiency. On actual Persuasion checks directed at a creature with an explicitly recorded character level lower than your total character level, gain advantage. NEW: compare true character levels, not CR, Hit Dice, faction standing, rank or apparent seniority. A creature with only CR and no character level is not qualified through a fabricated conversion; its Director can supply an actual level only if its real profile legitimately includes one. Check eligibility at the roll, without granting the speaker metagame disclosure of the hidden value. Equal or higher level gives no advantage from this clause. All actual social possibilities, agency and costs remain.
workedCases: A level8 speaker negotiating with an actual level5 NPC can gain advantage. An NPC listed only as CR5 is not silently treated as level5.
CHA +3 is used once on ordinary Intimidation. The feat does not make the total CHA +3 plus STR +2 or grant an extra +3.

currentPublic.name: Courtly Manners

sourceObject.name: Courtly Manners
sourceObject.description: You are well-versed in noble etiquette.
sourceObject.effect: You have advantage on Charisma checks when interacting with nobles and can gain audience with important figures more easily.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Gain advantage on actual Charisma ability checks when directly interacting with someone who genuinely holds a noble social position recognized by the current community. Preserve the source's breadth: it is not restricted to etiquette checks or friendly nobles. A Charisma attack or saving throw is not an ability check. NEW audience procedure: spend fifteen active minutes preparing and submitting one credible request through an actually accessible official, host or gatekeeper. Gain advantage on a Persuasion check to arrange an audience with an important figure even when that intermediary is not noble. The audience must be possible under the figure's actual schedule, policy and willingness; announce the attainable appointment and any fee, introduction or condition before rolling. Success secures that opportunity on those terms, not immediate entry, a title, waived security or agreement to the later request. A repeated identical petition to the same gatekeeper yields no new roll without a changed circumstance. Required identity, dress and communication remain actual resources.
workedCases: A noble's hostile interrogation can still qualify for the feat's advantage on an actual Charisma check made in that interaction; nobility does not guarantee a friendly response.
A successful gatekeeper petition secures the announced appointment tomorrow with its stated fee. It does not place the character in a closed chamber immediately.

sourceObject.effect: You gain proficiency with artisan's tools and can craft items in half the normal time.

currentPublic.operationalRules: NEW once per turn, after your direct attack with a weapon whose native damage includes bludgeoning hits, you may move the target5ft to a legal unoccupied destination, subject to a target size no more than one category larger than you. It cannot lift into unsupported air or through a wall; ordinary falling applies if moved over a real edge. Resolve hit damage before movement; an actual hit with0resolved damage can still qualify. A real natural weapon qualifies only if its profile is a bludgeoning weapon; ordinary unarmed is not one without an express rule.

sourceObject.description: Racial feat tied to Ogre heritage.
sourceObject.effect: Your melee hits knock targets back 5 feet if you're moving.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Require actual Ogre heritage. NEW once on your own original regular turn, after moving at least5ft of voluntary continuous movement directly toward a target immediately before your next personal melee attack against it, a hit may push it5ft directly away. The approach must use a real movement mode and paid path with no intervening action/attack/teleport/forced displacement; the attack itself is the endpoint. The melee attack can be weapon, unarmed or spell if otherwise legal. No extra movement, attack or damage. NEW no saving throw and target at most one size larger than your actual body, not Powerful Build; choose use after hit before resolving push. Resolve damage/immediate riders first; target must still exist and be legally movable. Push uses ordinary forced-movement collision, occupies legal space and stops before a barrier, never adds collision damage or ordinary opportunity attacks. If no legal positive displacement remains, no movement occurs and the chosen attempt remains used. Other independently qualified source pushes retain their exact stacking rules; this is no once-per-hit loop.

sourceObject.name: Cultural Expert
sourceObject.description: Studied history or lore receives the listed +2 bonus on related knowledge checks.
sourceObject.effect: Choose History, Religion, or a culture-specific Lore skill. Gain proficiency; if already proficient, add double your proficiency bonus to checks concerning cultures, customs, and historical context.
sourceObject.legacyEffect: Gain +2 on all knowledge checks involving history or lore
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: At acquisition choose History, Religion, or one specifically documented culture-specific Lore credential. If you are not proficient in the selected credential, gain its proficiency. If you already are, use twice PB for that credential's checks concerning cultures, customs and historical context; other checks in the selected skill retain normal PB. NEW: snapshot which branch applies on acquisition. Later gaining proficiency from another source does not retroactively convert the initial proficiency grant into Expertise. If a chosen culture has no separate recorded Lore credential, record a bounded History specialization for that named existing culture. It gives proficiency only for that subject, or twice PB there if History or that same subject is already proficient; it never creates general proficiency in a twenty-first skill. Double PB replaces rather than adds to normal PB and does not stack with other Expertise. Preserve actual access to knowledge and existing canon. No cosmological fact or cultural history is authored by choosing the feat.
workedCases: An already History-proficient holder uses twice PB for a check about a known people's treaty custom. The same feat supplies no proficiency multiplier to an Engineering check about the load-bearing capacity of a wall.
An untrained character chooses Religion and gains proficiency. A later duplicate Religion grant follows its own replacement rule; it does not silently upgrade this feat to Expertise.

currentPublic.name: Deceiver

sourceObject.name: Deceiver
sourceObject.description: You are a master of deception.
sourceObject.effect: You gain proficiency in Deception and can lie convincingly even under magical compulsion.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Gain Deception proficiency. NEW explicit source exception: you can deliberately speak a false assertion even while a magical effect would otherwise prohibit that assertion solely because it is a lie or require that assertion to be truthful. This is a narrow exception to truth-compulsion, including the lie-prohibition part of Zone of Truth, and must be approved against those exact spell records. You still make any actual save and remain subject to the effect's other clauses. It grants no automatic convincing success: resolve a real Deception check, opposed defense or other social procedure where required. It does not falsify memories, thoughts, directly revealed facts or independently recorded events; confer no blanket immunity to charm, compelled actions or orders; and does not let you avoid an order to speak or move when that obligation is separate from truthfulness. If another effect punishes actual lies, this feat permits the lie but does not negate its punishment. The caster receives only the information their source actually grants; the feat adds neither an automatic warning nor an undetectability guarantee.
workedCases: After failing a Zone of Truth save, the holder can attempt a deliberate verbal lie under this proposed exception. A suspicious listener may still defeat the Deception check.
A spell that directly reveals an actual memory is not changed by the holder speaking falsely. A separate penalty triggered by telling a lie still resolves.

currentPublic.name: Defender

sourceObject.name: Defender
sourceObject.description: You excel at protecting others.
sourceObject.effect: When an ally within 5 feet is attacked, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll.

currentPublic.operationalRules:
When an allied creature, including yourself, within5ft of you is targeted by an attack, spend Reaction before its attack roll to impose disadvantage on that one roll. NEW you must perceive the ally and the attacker's actual attack; no can-see requirement, shield or free hand is added, but you must be capable of a deliberate physical distraction/intervention with line of effect to the ally. It does not require reaching the attacker, so a visible incoming ranged shot can qualify. Range is checked at declaration and no movement is granted. Advantage cancels normally; later attacks in a multiattack need their own actual triggers/resources. This grants no damage transfer, interception, AC bonus or reroll after the result.
SOURCE SCOPE CORRECTION: “allies” includes the feat owner unless the actual clause says “other.” The owner must still meet the same hearing/perception, range, willing-target and action/resource predicates. No second body, observer or extra action is created by self-eligibility. This sentence supersedes any narrower owner-exclusion in the submitted proposal, not the preserved original.

currentPublic.name: Defensive Stance

sourceObject.name: Defensive Stance
sourceObject.description: You can adopt a defensive posture that greatly improves your protection.
sourceObject.effect: +15% AC, can't move this turn

currentPublic.operationalRules: NEW complete activation: when choosing your stance at the start of a regular own turn before using any stance benefit or moving voluntarily, choose Defensive Stance instead of a normal stance. No Action; one stance choice. Through your next original regular start, add floor(15% of your otherwise-current AC), minimum0, to AC. Compute the base after actual armor/shield/DEX/flat bonuses/penalties but before this or any other percentage-AC bonus; no percent-on-percent multiplication. Recompute when that underlying base changes, including conditional Guard. You cannot voluntarily change position by Speed expenditure, teleport or a feature while the current regular turn lasts; linked extra turns also retain the movement restriction. Standing/dropping Prone is allowed if ordinary budget/capability permits. Forced displacement remains possible and does not end the stance. Off-turn voluntary Reaction movement after that turn is allowed; AC lasts to expiry. It cannot coexist with Aggressive, Guarded, Mobile, Focused or Carrying because it occupies their stance choice, not a free extra buff.
workedCases: Underlying AC17 gains floor2.55=2, total19. The feat does not round to a3-point bonus.
A forced push during the stance moves the owner normally. They cannot then voluntarily teleport during their turn, but the push does not remove AC.

sourceObject.name: Disarm
sourceObject.description: You can disarm opponents in combat.
sourceObject.effect: You can attempt to disarm an opponent as an attack. The target makes a Strength or Dexterity save (DC 8 + proficiency + ability modifier).

currentPublic.operationalRules: Replace one attack of your Attack Action with this attempt against a held reachable object of a creature in your current melee reach. Failure drops one declared object to a legal adjacent unoccupied space you choose, otherwise its own space; success keeps it. Implanted body parts, worn armor and strapped shields are not freely held droppable objects. You do not gain custody automatically; retrieving costs normal interaction/time. No special proficiency requirement grants missing weapon PB on other attacks.

sourceObject.name: Disarming Blow
sourceObject.description: A Strength-trained melee combatant gains the listed chance to knock away a weapon.
sourceObject.effect: When you hit a creature holding an object, forgo one damage die to force a Strength or Dexterity save (target’s choice) against DC 8 + proficiency bonus + your attack ability modifier. On a failure, it drops one held object.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: On a hit with a melee weapon attack, before rolling damage, select one held reachable object and forgo one actual base-weapon damage die to attempt disarming it. NEW remove one die before critical doubling; a critical1d8 weapon forgoes its entire doubled base2d8, retaining lawful flat damage and independent riders. Never pay with a rider die, a die already spent on another feat, or a fixed-damage expression. The target chooses STR or DEX save against DC8+PB+the actual attack ability modifier. Resolve remaining hit damage, then the save if the creature still holds the object. Failure drops it into an adjacent legal unoccupied space you choose, otherwise its own space. No extra damage to object, severed curse or bond; actual non-droppable bonds prevent dropping. An object wielded with two hands is still one object. No new once-turn cap: each separately paid qualifying hit can attempt, but the chosen die is spent even if immunity prevents the result.

sourceObject.name: Disguise Expert
sourceObject.description: Practiced deception adds the listed +5 when the character is disguised.
sourceObject.effect: While wearing a prepared disguise, add +2 to Deception checks made to maintain the assumed identity. Creating a convincing disguise requires appropriate materials and 10 minutes.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Spend ten actual minutes preparing a physically plausible assumed identity using sufficient actual clothing, cosmetics, props and appropriate tools for the chosen disguise. Record its identity, wearer, materials and limitations. The feat owner gains +2 to their Deception checks to maintain that identity while actually wearing the prepared disguise; creating a disguise for another person does not give that wearer this feat's bonus. NEW: an existing prepared disguise made by another competent person can qualify when the holder wears it as intended. A disguise does not alter body size, anatomy, voice, knowledge, language, credentials or magical signature unless another source actually does. Detection uses the actual encounter's check and observer; success in preparation is not permanent immunity to inspection. Ordinary materials grant no extra numerical modifier. A reviewed tailored garment's own disguise/task bonus keeps its separate documented family and wearer restrictions. A ruined or incompatible disguise ceases to qualify until legally repaired or prepared again.
workedCases: The feat owner prepares an ally's disguise in ten minutes; the ally gets the physical disguise but no borrowed +2. The owner wearing their own prepared disguise receives +2 on the actual identity-maintenance check.
A small disguise cannot make a Large creature fit a human-sized doorway or supply a password. A successful clothing deception does not resolve either obstacle.

currentPublic.name: Distorted Dominance

sourceObject.name: Distorted Dominance
sourceObject.description: Your aberrant nature overwhelms enemy actions.
sourceObject.effect: Enemies who fail saves vs your effects also lose 1 action

currentPublic.operationalRules: NEW select the Warrior4 counterpart's Reaction denial, explicitly replacing the standalone oneAction loss for this proposal. Require an Aberrant mutation equipped and at least the actual generating Aberrant mutation active. When an actual hostile fails a save against your directly applied Aberrant mutation effect, it loses its Reaction through the end of its next future regular turn. This is triggered, costs no extra action, and is once per actual target per encounter across both catalog representations. Range/target legality comes from that mutation, not an additional universal aura. Source immunity/prevention blocks the applicable rider; do not add Charmed, Stunned, silence, Speed0 or new hard denial. A failed save against an unrelated spell, ally effect, periodic damage without a save or equipped-but-dormant mutation does not qualify. No loss of normalAction or guarantee of surrender. Retain the broader original whole-Action-denial wording as the explicitly rejected historical alternative. Adopt this bounded Reaction-denial procedure for the feat candidate; no class record is promoted or overwritten.

currentPublic.name: Divine Favor

sourceObject.name: Divine Favor
sourceObject.description: You have earned the favor of a deity.
sourceObject.effect: Once per long rest, you can call upon divine aid to automatically succeed on one saving throw or ability check.

currentPublic.operationalRules:
Retain CHA15 and an actual already established worship-of-a-deity credential without selecting a new deity or interpreting doctrine here. NEW once per beneficial Long Rest, after your own actual saving throw or ability check is called for, or after its result is known but before its consequences commit, declare this feat to replace that one outcome with ordinary Success. No Action, component or new roll is required; it can protect a living incapacitated creature making an actual save, including a death save. It cannot act after death or reverse committed harm. Fixed-DC task outcome becomes Success, not Critical Success; saves become successful without a natural face or a success-by-margin value. A death save gains one ordinary success, not natural20healing. For a genuinely authorized crafting completion check, this means Standard success in that craft procedure, retaining all work/material/access requirements and any independently reviewed quality adjustment.

For your side of an actual opposed ability check, NEW it wins against an ordinary rolled opponent regardless of total. If both sides commit an explicit automatic-success effect to the same opposition, resolve their incompatible claims by preserving the existing state, as with the Core initiating-tie rule; no retroactive transfer of an already resolved result. This declared conflict rule needs joint review. The feat does not create an ability check when none is allowed, overcome physical impossibility, convert an attack into a check, grant NPC consent outside a legitimately established social success outcome, or grant knowledge unavailable to the legal task. Only one check/save is affected; another save from the same damage event remains separate. Other outcome-triggered rules see ordinary Success, no natural20/1 and no invented numerical margin.
workedCases: A living dying character is about to record its third death-save failure. Spending this feat before that failure commits replaces it with one success; it does not restore1HP or erase earlier counters.

A qualified craft completion would fail after all its real work. The feat gives Standard success, not automatic Masterwork or free ingredients. An impossible request with no authorized check cannot be made possible by spending it.

currentPublic.name: Draw Cut

sourceObject.name: Draw Cut
sourceObject.description: Quick blade work increases damage when a weapon is unsheathed.
sourceObject.effect: Once per encounter, when you draw a sheathed melee weapon as part of an attack, add one weapon damage die on a hit.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Once per encounter, when you legally draw a genuinely sheathed melee weapon as part of making a weapon attack with it, declare Draw Cut before the attack roll. NEW drawing uses the normal free object interaction or another explicitly granted draw permission; this feat grants no extra hand or interaction. The weapon must actually be secured in a sheath/scabbard, not merely dropped, held or conjured. A hit adds one actual base weapon die before critical doubling. A miss spends the declaration and encounter use. Resheathing, switching weapons, initiative exits and new turns do not refresh it. The attack may be a thrown attack with that melee weapon if drawing and throwing are otherwise legal. No attack Action or BA is supplied by the feat.
workedCases: Drawing a1d6 shortsword into a critical adds one base d6 and doubles both base dice for4d6.
After a missed Draw Cut, sheathing and drawing a second weapon during the same fight cannot restore the use.

currentPublic.name: Dual Wielder

sourceObject.name: Dual Wielder
sourceObject.description: You master fighting with two weapons.
sourceObject.effect: You can use two-weapon fighting with non-light weapons and gain +1 AC while wielding two weapons.

currentPublic.operationalRules: For ordinary two-weapon fighting, each weapon may be a non-Light one-handed melee weapon that you can actually wield in its own usable hand. Do not dual-wield a weapon requiring two hands with another weapon absent an actual specific hand exception. Gain+1AC while actually wielding two such usable melee weapons, one in each of two hands; a Broken, stowed, dropped or anatomy-incompatible weapon cannot supply the bonus. No extra draw/stow, BA or positive offhand damage modifier: Ambidexterity or another explicit grant supplies that separately. The ordinary Attack Action and two-weapon BA trigger remain.

currentPublic.name: Dungeon Cartographer

sourceObject.name: Dungeon Cartographer
sourceObject.description: An experienced explorer builds a map while moving through a dungeon.
sourceObject.effect: You can create reliable maps while traveling at a normal pace. After mapping an area for 10 minutes, you and allies using the map gain advantage on checks to retrace that route until the dungeon reshapes it.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Use actual recording tools and observable route evidence to map while moving at the adopted normal travel pace. This expressly permits that narrow concurrent mapping; it does not permit another incompatible Watch job. NEW: track ten accumulated active minutes on one identified continuous route or area, pausing when unable to observe or record. After those minutes, the resulting map grants advantage to you and allies actually using an accurate accessible copy on checks whose purpose is retracing its recorded route. It conveys no unseen passage, secret door, current occupant or guaranteed safety. The map remains useful until the route is reshaped or materially changed; mark changed segments unreliable while preserving still-valid observations. A map of one path cannot supply advantage to another. The feat does not grant normal-pace stealth, foraging, scouting or unlimited movement.
workedCases: Six observable mapping minutes, a five-minute obscured halt, and four more observable minutes complete the ten-minute route record; the halt counts on the world clock but not as mapping.
After one bridge collapses, the old map can still guide the intact approach. It cannot grant advantage to cross the missing bridge or prove an unobserved alternate route exists.

currentPublic.name: Dungeon Delver

sourceObject.name: Dungeon Delver
sourceObject.description: You are experienced in underground exploration.
sourceObject.effect: You have advantage on Perception and Investigation checks to detect secret doors and traps.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Gain advantage on actual Perception or Investigation checks whose purpose is detecting a secret door or a trap. Use Perception to notice accessible sensory clues and Investigation to examine and interpret the actual mechanism or evidence, as the task warrants; do not add both skill proficiencies or roll both automatically. NEW: the feat's advantage changes active rolls only. It does not add a passive+5 or create a passive Investigation procedure by itself. Actual light, senses, range, access and search time remain; a completely inaccessible or undetectable feature is not revealed by an uncalled-for roll. Success reveals the detection information defined by that task, not automatic disarming, a save bonus, damage resistance, magical identification or immunity to a trigger encountered while searching. Trap Sense and Observant are separate feats with their own actual passive grants.
workedCases: An actual Investigation search of a suspicious hinge gains advantage. The same check does not disarm a linked trap unless a separate procedure actually does that.
A passive Perception of15 remains15 from this feat alone; there is no invented+5 for advantage. Separately owned Observant would have its own modifier.

currentPublic.name: Durable

sourceObject.name: Durable
sourceObject.description: Hardy and resilient, you gain the following benefits:
sourceObject.effect: Increase Constitution by 1, when you roll a Hit Die to regain hit points, minimum amount regained equals twice your Constitution modifier

currentPublic.operationalRules: Increase Constitution by 1, normally no higher than 20, and recompute the real derived modifier and maximum-HP records without healing. For each actual Hit Die legally spent and rolled to restore HP, NEW: set that die's pre-healing-modifier amount to the greatest of its ordinary die-plus-CON healing amount, twice the current signed CON modifier, and zero. Apply the minimum after the ordinary die-plus-CON calculation, separately per die, before ordinary healing bonuses, reductions, blockers and maximum/Critical caps. The resulting actual HP gain may be less than this raw minimum or zero. It creates no Hit Die, rest permission or automatic restoration of spent dice. unchangedReviewedRecord.operationalRules:
## Empowered Summoning — Magic; Charisma14+

When your actual source activation genuinely creates a new finite summoned creature, offer it `2 × your PB at creation` temporary HP. Its lifetime is default recipient long rest, also ending when that creature instance ends. Returned/revived preexisting bodies, persistent companion redeploy/rebuild, Mage bound returns, Ranger bonds and devices do not qualify merely by appearing again.

Record a lineage key containing the owner, actual source activation root and creation-slot/body-lineage. Several distinct bodies created by one source each receive their own grant. Reissuing/recreating the same lineage never refreshes its creation grant or its round damage entitlement. A genuinely new activation paid/used under its own rules can create a new root. An Action, limited use, ritual use or item charge can be a real source cost; RP is not mandatory.

Each qualifying creature adds its owner's **current PB** to its first actual damage roll in each canonical round/window. Add this flat bonus once to a shared area roll, not once per affected target. A roll on an ongoing damage tick can qualify; fixed damage without a roll does not consume or receive the rider. Later rolls in that window gain nothing. sourceObject.name: Enchantment Focus
sourceObject.description: Your enchantment spells are more effective.
sourceObject.effect: Creatures have disadvantage on saving throws against your enchantment spells.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Require actual access to a spell cast through an Enchantment placement. Creatures have disadvantage on actual saving throws against spells you personally cast through their Enchantment school/mode. NEW this includes initial and later repeat saves belonging to that same Enchantment cast, for its actual duration; it includes a qualifying spell-cast item/feat route whose actual recorded school is Enchantment. A same-name Illusion or Universal placement is not Enchantment merely because another class has that school. Apply ordinary advantage/disadvantage cancellation, not an extra die per feat or repeated disadvantage. Actual control immunity, target restrictions, voluntary-save rules, information protection and automatic ending remain. A separate CONconcentration save caused by an Enchantment spell’s damage is a save to maintain the target’s own concentration, not a save against your spell, and receives no disadvantage from this feat. Ability checks, opposed social rolls and nonspell class techniques are outside its scope.

currentPublic.name: Endurance

sourceObject.name: Endurance
sourceObject.description: You can push your body beyond normal limits.
sourceObject.effect: You can go twice as long without food, water, or sleep, and you have advantage on Constitution saves against exhaustion.

currentPublic.operationalRules:
Keep advantage on an actual Constitution save to resist Exhaustion; this supplies no save where the governing rule assesses a penalty directly. NEW Endurance/EX58 bridge: keep the same 24-hour provisioning checkpoints, eight-hour Watches, two-active-work ceiling, actual Rest Debt opening, deadline at the end of the second following Watch, and safe eight-hour rest cure. Do not double a Watch, create food/water, lengthen an actual sleep-debt deadline, or treat work as rest.
Maintain two separate feat records, foodWaterPending and sleepPending, each initially 0 and limited to 0 or 1. At a canonical daily checkpoint where food/water shortage is the sole reason for the one expedition-Strain penalty, 0 becomes 1 and that one penalty is omitted; 1 becomes 0 and the original one penalty applies. A day actually meeting both food and water requirements clears foodWaterPending. Another unmet mandatory logistical requirement still causes its original single daily penalty; Endurance does not reduce it or add a second daily penalty. The day remains unsupported wherever its actual requirements are unmet, even when the feat omits a Strain point.
At an actual canonical sleep-debt penalty event, apply the same 0→1/omit, 1→0/apply sequence to sleepPending. Assess each original event once: the unpaid deadline event and a subsequent missed designated Rest Watch follow their own EX58 scheduling; do not create an hourly or per-Watch penalty. Debt remains owed and deadlines reset only as EX58 says. A genuinely completed safe eight-hour rest clears sleepPending and actual Rest Debt, even if it supplies no additional beneficial-long-rest resource recovery. Food/water and sleep credits never offset each other. Other Strain, Exhaustion, air, weather and hazard causes retain their original rules.
Acquisition clears neither existing Strain nor existing debt. If the feat is unavailable at a checkpoint, apply the original cause-specific penalty and clear that cause's pending credit; availability later cannot rewrite the past. Preserve all assessed and omitted events and their causes. This is an explicitly NEW interpretation of 'go twice as long': it halves the frequency of the applicable canonical penalty events, not the elapsed length of every irregular sleep-debt window. Literal older wording and the rejected generic-timer draft remain historical.
workedCases: A standard actor lacks water but has all other daily provisions. At the first 24-hour shortage checkpoint Endurance omits the one Strain point and sets foodWaterPending=1; at the next equally unsupported checkpoint it applies one and returns the counter to0. Both days are still unsupported; no water or recovery permission appears.

A missed Rest Watch opens actual Rest Debt. At its unchanged deadline Endurance may omit its first sleep penalty, but the debt is not cleared. A later canonical missed-Rest penalty applies the second point and resets only the normal EX58 deadline. A real safe eight-hour rest clears the debt and sleepPending, not a previously spent RP pool or another beneficial-long-rest allowance.

sourceObject.name: Energy Sink
sourceObject.description: Hard-won magical resilience restores RP after a spell strikes.
sourceObject.effect: When you succeed on a saving throw against a spell or take no damage from it, use your reaction to recover 1 RP. You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.
sourceObject.legacyEffect: Restore mana when hit by spells
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules:
PB uses per completed LR; no mid-epoch refill fromPBgrowth. After one actual hostile spell event targeting/affecting you resolves, if you either succeeded on its real save OR received no positive resolved damage from that event, you may spend a Reaction/use to recover 1 RP up to your real maximum. NEW require meaningful unwilling opposition: harmless, allied, cooperative, self-authored or farming spells do not qualify. A spell attack that legally targeted you but missed, immunity, or complete prevention can satisfy the no-damage branch; temp HP absorption is damage and alone cannot. A failed save against a hostile nondamaging control spell still satisfies literal no-damage, but only if its result leaves you able to react. One grant per actual cast identity across later ticks/events; no fan-out or repeating-zone farm. Positive saved-against damage may qualify through success. Resolve full damage/control/death first; no ordinary Reaction at 0 HP. Decline before spending if noRPheadroom. This is recovery, not transfer from the attacker or a new pool.
For this trigger, actual damage includes damage absorbed by Temp HP, so a spell that damages only Temp HP is not a no-damage event. A genuine ward that prevents all damage may leave a qualifying original hostile spell event; the ward does not itself generate a second event. Every explicit no-resource source flag remains controlling; see FS-07.
workedCases: Successful save halves a hostile spell to 5 damage: the success branch permits oneReaction for 1 RP.
A missed hostile spell attack can qualify; receiving a friendly harmless cantrip cannot.

reviewedAcquisitionDescriptor.completeControllingOperativeProcedure:
PB uses per completed LR; no mid-epoch refill fromPBgrowth. After one actual hostile spell event targeting/affecting you resolves, if you either succeeded on its real save OR received no positive resolved damage from that event, you may spend a Reaction/use to recover 1 RP up to your real maximum. NEW require meaningful unwilling opposition: harmless, allied, cooperative, self-authored or farming spells do not qualify. A spell attack that legally targeted you but missed, immunity, or complete prevention can satisfy the no-damage branch; temp HP absorption is damage and alone cannot. A failed save against a hostile nondamaging control spell still satisfies literal no-damage, but only if its result leaves you able to react. One grant per actual cast identity across later ticks/events; no fan-out or repeating-zone farm. Positive saved-against damage may qualify through success. Resolve full damage/control/death first; no ordinary Reaction at 0 HP. Decline before spending if noRPheadroom. This is recovery, not transfer from the attacker or a new pool.
For this trigger, actual damage includes damage absorbed by Temp HP, so a spell that damages only Temp HP is not a no-damage event. A genuine ward that prevents all damage may leave a qualifying original hostile spell event; the ward does not itself generate a second event. Every explicit no-resource source flag remains controlling; see FS-07.

currentPublic.name: Entertainer

sourceObject.name: Entertainer
sourceObject.description: You can captivate audiences.
sourceObject.effect: You gain proficiency in Performance and can earn money and gather information through performances.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Gain Performance proficiency. NEW finite work procedure: arrange a real two-hour performance booking with an accessible venue, an actual audience and a willing payer, using the necessary real instrument, props or voice. The default mundane fee for this proposed booking is2sp, quoted and agreed before work; an actual negotiated contract may specify another amount or a performance standard. Complete the two active hours to earn the contractual payment from that payer, minus any actual venue costs. If the contract makes pay contingent on a check, state that DC and failure payment before accepting. During one fifteen-minute audience interaction within that booking, make Charisma (Performance) DC12 to engage attendees; on success one willing attendee offers an actual relevant local event, contact or rumor from their knowledge. Label hearsay and uncertainty; no attendee with relevant information means no invented rumor. The booking can coexist with that expressly allowed conversation, not another work action or rest. Repeating for the same unchanged audience gives no new information roll; a new booking needs real demand and payment. Record spent time, patron and money so no repeated-roll income is created.
workedCases: One completed2sp booking with5cp venue costs nets15cp. It consumes two actual hours and the payer's actual2sp, not an unlimited roll reward.
A successful performance for an audience that knows no relevant news creates no hidden fact. A later identical song to those same attendees does not reset their information.

sourceObject.name: Ether Anchor
sourceObject.description: At level 12, an anchored presence resists banishment effects.
sourceObject.effect: You have advantage on saving throws against banishment, forced teleportation, and planar displacement. Once per long rest, you may choose to succeed on one such save.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: At character level 12, gain advantage on actual saving throws against an effect that would banish, forcibly teleport or displace you between planes. Once LR, after such a save fails but before consequences, optionally replace that failure with success; use the source’s actual success outcome, which may retain other effects. No Action or Reaction is required. It does not create a save against a save-less effect, convert willing travel to hostility, anchor nearby creatures, reveal destinations or permit an otherwise illegal movement. A save against damage accompanying independent displacement qualifies only if that same save actually determines the unwanted displacement. Existing explicit unpreventable/no-replacement rules control. No permanent immunity or new cosmological fact is implied.

currentPublic.name: Fast Talker

sourceObject.name: Fast Talker
sourceObject.description: You can talk your way out of trouble.
sourceObject.effect: You can attempt to distract or confuse enemies with rapid speech, potentially causing them to lose their action.

currentPublic.operationalRules: NEW complete combat procedure: Action, once per SR, choose one hostile creature within30ft that can hear your rapid speech and understands the language you actually speak. Spend the use at declaration; it makesWIS save DC8+PB+CHA. Failure prevents it taking an Action during its next future regular turn; movement, BA and Reaction are not otherwise removed, and an extra-Action grant cannot bypass that turn's denial. The source-character/target/encounter hard-denial guard applies jointly with class/spell/companion/other feat denial; a target already affected by your hard denial in this encounter cannot suffer this rider again. NEW hearing/language comprehension and a capacity to process speech are required; explicit immunity to this mental action-denial effect blocks it, but the feat does not automatically impose Charmed, Frightened or Stunned. It neither forces beliefs nor commands a particular act. Outside combat it can support an ordinary social attempt but does not automatically win agreement or impose a recurring lost-time penalty.
workedCases: A hearing language-sharing foe failsDC14: it can move and use a legalBA on its next regular turn, but cannot take an Action.
A foe unable to understand the speech is ineligible, and a previously denied target is protected by the shared encounter guard.

currentPublic.name: Feint

sourceObject.name: Feint
sourceObject.description: You can mislead opponents with deceptive movements.
sourceObject.effect: Enemy loses AC vs next attack

currentPublic.operationalRules: NEW complete procedure: Bonus Action, one perceived hostile creature within30ft that can perceive your deliberate threatening movement; oppose your CHA Deception with its WIS Insight. Higher total wins; ties preserve state, with no task-degree/natural shift. On success, apply−2AC against your next attack on that creature before your next original regular start. Declare the affected attack before rolling; it consumes the feint hit or miss. Failure has no effect. Only one unspent Feint per owner; a new successful Feint replaces your prior mark. Multiple owners can each set their own next-attack records, but one attack never receives more than one−2 Feint layer. Feint does not compel beliefs, create a universal off-guard condition or lower AC against other attackers. No rest use cap; the real BA and opposed check fund each attempt. If a target cannot perceive the act, it is ineligible rather than automatically beaten.
workedCases: Deception17 defeats Insight14. The owner's next attack checks AC16 instead of18 and consumes the mark even on a miss.
An ally attacks first: that attack gains no Feint bonus and does not consume the owner's mark.

currentPublic.name: Fencer

sourceObject.name: Fencer
sourceObject.description: You are skilled with finesse weapons.
sourceObject.effect: When wielding a finesse weapon, you gain +1 AC and can make opportunity attacks when enemies enter your reach.

currentPublic.operationalRules: While actually wielding a usable Finesse melee weapon, gain+1AC as one feat modifier. NEW a second empty hand is not required and a lawful shield may coexist; the weapon must remain wielded with actual anatomy and cannot be Broken/stowed. When a seen hostile creature voluntarily crosses from outside to inside that weapon's ordinary current melee reach, you may spend Reaction for one opportunity attack with that same weapon immediately after entry and before further movement. It must be a legal melee target in reach then. Forced displacement, teleport, newly appearing, your movement/reach expansion and the target merely starting within reach do not trigger. Disengage/opportunity immunity suppresses it. Lunge's single-attack extension creates no persistent entry boundary. No additional Reaction or perpetual threatened range.

sourceObject.description: You have fey blood in your lineage.
sourceObject.effect: You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed, and magic can't put you to sleep.

unchangedReviewedRecord.acquisition: Actual class feat selection; source-specific prerequisite at acquisition
unchangedReviewedRecord.operationalRules:
## Field Medic — General; trained in Medicine

As a Bonus Action, use one actual healer's-kit use on one legally reachable living dying creature. Resolve the canonical automatic kit stabilization, including its normal1d4-hour recovery deadline. Inventory must contain a real remaining use; this feat invents no kit capacity. This is distinct from the ordinary Action/DC10 Wisdom(Medicine) stabilization option.

Whenever you actually cause a dying→Stable transition by **any legal method**, offer the target your PB temporary HP with default lifetime. Record the transition when it occurs. Already-Stable creatures cannot be stabilized again for a new grant. Record one entitlement per target + actual dying episode + feat owner, plus the actual stabilization event ID. Different owners do not share an artificial family lock, but each must actually cause a valid transition. A new episode requires a genuine exit from the old dying episode and later entry into dying; damage absorbed entirely by temporary HP does not create one.

If you also possess Battlefield Medic's separately sourced Trauma Response, first record the actual kit stabilization, then resolve that background's independent1HP recovery, then resolve Field Medic's temporary-HP offer. The later1HP does not erase the stabilization trigger. The feat itself provides no normal HP, consciousness, Wound removal or resurrection. No background is granted by acquiring this feat.

**NEW integration:** event/episode anti-replay identity and ordering with independent recovery; the broad “when you stabilize” trigger is preserved.

sourceObject.name: Field Surgeon
sourceObject.description: A Wisdom-trained medic uses Medicine to stabilize an ally at 1 HP.
sourceObject.effect: When you successfully stabilize a dying creature with Medicine or a healer’s kit, it regains 1 hit point. A creature can benefit from this feat once per long rest.
sourceObject.legacyEffect: Stabilize ally with 1 HP using Medicine
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: When you actually cause a living dying creature to become Stable by a legal Medicine stabilization or a real healer's-kit use, offer that recipient 1 HP. Use the ordinary Action/DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) route or the ordinary Action/one-kit-use route; an independently owned feature may explicitly change that action cost. NEW: treat the 1 HP as a direct state-recovery grant following the completed stabilization, not ordinary rolled healing. Broad cannot-regain-HP restrictions and the living-target gate apply; it receives no ordinary healing bonuses. Record one Field-Surgeon-family entitlement per recipient's own completed-long-rest epoch, shared across all practitioners. Commit it on the eligible offer even when HP gain is blocked. The actual stabilization remains recorded; if recovery is blocked the creature stays Stable at 0 with its normal existing recovery deadline. If positive HP is gained, clear the obsolete Stable deadline normally. A separately owned Field Medic temp-HP offer still uses the genuine stabilization event, even if the recipient is now at 1 HP. Already Stable or dead creatures create no new trigger.
workedCases: Medicine succeeds for a dying recipient: record stabilization, then recover 1 HP and end zero-HP unconsciousness if no independent cause remains. A later practitioner cannot supply a second Field Surgeon point before that recipient completes a long rest.
Decay blocks HP gain: the recipient remains Stable 0 and the feat entitlement is spent. Field Medic may still offer its separately legal temporary HP, which do not wake the recipient.

Preserve, transport and consume the actual output normally.

These are food/water only, not seven complete Supply Units: no oil, sundries, storage or transport is awarded. currentPublic.name: Forensic Investigator

sourceObject.name: Forensic Investigator
sourceObject.description: Investigative training reveals the listed hidden clues from a scene.
sourceObject.effect: When examining a scene for at least 10 minutes, the Director must reveal one additional physical clue that could reasonably be discovered there on a successful Investigation check.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Spend at least ten active minutes examining an identified scene with actual senses, light, physical access and tools appropriate to the proposed search. Then resolve its Intelligence (Investigation) task and ordinary consequences. On Success or Critical Success, reveal one additional physical clue that could reasonably have been discovered in the searched evidence, beyond the ordinary success information. NEW: before resolving the check, the Director records a finite eligible extra clue or that no further physical evidence is available. If none exists, say so; do not invent evidence or refund the elapsed time. Interpretations are distinguished from observations. Repeating an unchanged search, sharing the result or adding a second feat owner cannot clone the same clue into a new fact. A new area, technique, access or evidence can justify a different examination. Destroyed or moved evidence must actually be available to the method used.
workedCases: Ordinary success finds a forced lock; the feat additionally reveals an actual distinctive metal shaving caught in the frame. It cannot name the unknown culprit without evidence.
A thoroughly washed empty chamber may yield no surviving additional clue. Success confirms that no further physical clue is available to this examination; it does not create footprints.

currentPublic.name: Foresight Surge

sourceObject.name: Foresight Surge
sourceObject.description: After casting divination, foresight grants the listed initiative increase.
sourceObject.effect: After you cast a divination spell, gain +2 initiative for the next hour. If initiative is already rolled, move up one place in the order at the start of the next round.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules:
After a completed actual Divination cast, gain a nonstacking+2 to future initiative rolls for one elapsed hour, refreshing that deadline on later eligible casts. The selected casting class must use Divination for this identity. If already participating in rolled initiative, also queue one move up one baseline place at the next numbered-round boundary. NEW one queued move per owner per boundary; repeated casts cannot accumulate jumps. At that boundary finish previous-round events, restore temporary permutations, then process pending advances in stable activation order by swapping the owner with the immediately preceding still-participating baseline actor; top actor stays. Apply later reviewed temporary permutations, such as Future Echo, to the resulting baseline. Every participant still receives one regular slot. A departed actor without a retained initiative slot loses its pending advance without makeup. Incapacitation alone does not remove an actor’s regular slot or this pending ordering change. Existing virtual deadlines, recharge, periodic clocks and spent budgets do not move or refresh; no reroll or extra turn.
For actual Future Echo, restore an expiring permutation first, apply this feat’s pending baseline advances once in the stated stable order, then apply a newly established Future Echo permutation to the resulting baseline. Preserve actual slots and spent turns; no extra turn or resource refresh occurs.
workedCases: OrderA, B, C withCqueued becomesA, C, B next round;Cdoes not act again in the current round.
Three Divination casts before that boundary still queue only one advance forC.

sourceObject.description: Racial feat tied to Dwarf heritage.
sourceObject.effect: Forged – All crafted armor has +10% durability and you resist fire by +10%.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Require actual Dwarf heritage. NEW: when you are the lead and personally complete a newly crafted armor suit, record a P10 physical durability workmanship source on that exact output. “All crafted armor” means your own completed outputs, including a lawful transformative recipe whose actual armor host qualifies; purchased suits or merely repaired suits do not acquire it. Shields are excluded unless an exact armor profile expressly includes them. Use the reviewed strongest percentage workmanship family: P10 competes with P25/P50 rather than multiplying. Compute baselineB after actual size/grade, improved maximum B+max(1,floor(B×P/100)) for positiveP, apply any persistent flaw last, and preserve the actual damage deficit. This is permanent physical workmanship, unaffected by magic suppression, with no automatic current-HP healing beyond the existing capacity/deficit calculation. Separately, your personal fire-damage defense is explicitly10%, not standard half resistance. NEW: after ordinary fire immunity/resistance/vulnerability and other passive flat reductions, multiply the remaining nonnegative fire component by0.90 and round down once for this step before later eligible reactions/tempHP. One Forge instance applies once; it does not improve another creature wearing your armor or turn your fire defense into20%.

An11-fire component becomes5 after normal resistance and its normal rounding, then4 after Forge’s0.90 step. A companion wearing your forged armor gains its workmanship, not your personal fire defense.

currentPublic.name: Giant Strength

sourceObject.name: Giant Strength
sourceObject.description: You possess the strength of giants.
sourceObject.effect: Your carrying capacity doubles, and you can wield weapons one size larger than normal without penalty.

currentPublic.operationalRules: After computing the current body's ordinary physical carrying capacity and inventory Load capacity from actual Strength and size, double both capacities. NEW: the same factor also doubles the corresponding push/drag/lift limit so that the paired physical-handling limits remain coherent. It does not double an item's weight, remove carried cargo, alter casualty Load, enlarge a mount's capacity or multiply an already modified result twice. Distinct capacity effects use their actual stacking clauses; no generic repeated doubling is granted. You may wield a weapon made for a body one size category larger than your actual current body without a size-only handling penalty. Use that weapon's actual reviewed item profile, hands, reach, damage and properties; the feat itself adds no damage die, reach, proficiency, free hand or two-size permission. An oversized weapon without a complete source profile remains an item-authoring dependency rather than receiving improvised bigger statistics. Real anatomy and Strength requirements still apply.
workedCases: A Medium STR-18 body has ordinary 270-pound carry and 18 Load; this proposal gives 540 pounds and 36 Load, with the corresponding lift/push/drag limit doubled once.
Wielding an actual Large weapon does not give a Medium holder Large reach or an extra damage die unless that weapon's complete profile expressly supplies it.

sourceObject.description: Racial feat tied to Feykin heritage.
sourceObject.effect: Enemies attacking you for the first time have a 20% miss chance.

NEW for each actual hostile identity in one real encounter, its first legally declared attack against you faces a20% miss check: roll1d100 once,1–20 makes that attack miss,21–100 proceeds normally. Commit the attacker's action, ammunition and source costs first, then roll this check before its ordinary attack die or automatic-hit resolution. The first legal attack consumes that attacker's encounter record even if the percentage check succeeds or its later attack roll would miss. No record is spent by an illegal/out-of-range declaration. A blocked first attack has no on-hit/critical result, but actual miss riders can operate. For a multiattack sequence only its first attack faces this roll; one attack with several components faces one check. No sight requirement on either combatant is invented. Leaving/reentering, disguise, charm changes or a new form of the same attacker never resets the record. This is a supernatural feat defense with no creature-type, invisibility or cosmology grant.

currentPublic.name: Healer

sourceObject.name: Healer
sourceObject.description: You are skilled in medicine and healing.
sourceObject.effect: You can use a healer's kit to restore hit points and stabilize dying creatures more effectively.

currentPublic.operationalRules: NEW full healing procedure: as an Action, spend one real healer's-kit charge to treat one adjacent legally reachable living creature. Choose ordinary stabilization only, or this feat's healing treatment. A full actual kit has ten charges, costs 5 gp and weighs 3 lb under the reviewed item rule; transfer or partial use never refills it. Healing treatment has one entitlement per recipient per that recipient's completed short or long rest, shared across all Healer practitioners. Commit that entitlement and the charge before resolution even if healing is later blocked. If the recipient is dying, first cause an actual dying-to-Stable transition using this paid kit use, then resolve ordinary healing of 2d4 plus the practitioner's signed Wisdom modifier, minimum zero before the normal healing pipeline. One charge funds both parts of this single treatment. If HP gain is blocked, the stabilization remains with its genuine recovery deadline; if positive HP returns, close that obsolete deadline normally. A recipient whose healing entitlement is spent may still receive ordinary kit stabilization for its real charge and Action, without more feat HP. Already Stable creatures can receive the once-per-rest healing but create no new stabilization trigger. This removes no Wounds, Injury, disease or death. Independently owned Field Medic/Field Surgeon triggers require their actual source/event and own limits, with no duplicated kit charge or invented second stabilization.
workedCases: One charge treats a dying target: record stabilization, then dice 3+2 and WIS +3 give 8 ordinary healing before actual modifiers/caps. A second Healer owner cannot repeat the HP treatment before that target rests.

The feat supplies this one specific salve, not access to the separately reviewed Herbalism formulas, their quality/yield/XP, or unlimited supplies. sourceObject.description: You age more slowly than normal.
sourceObject.effect: You age at half the normal rate and have advantage on death saving throws.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Require Constitution 17 and total character level 10. From acquisition onward, accrue natural biological aging at half the body's otherwise applicable natural rate. NEW: keep elapsed world time and accumulated age separate; the feat does not reverse existing age or halve a discrete magical aging event unless that event expressly changes the natural aging rate. sourceObject.name: Improved Athlete
sourceObject.description: Your athletic abilities are exceptional.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Requires the actual Athlete feat, ID athlete. Gain climbing and swimming Speeds equal to current legal walking Speed; alternate sources granting those same modes do not add together. NEW reading of the source's unrestricted long-jump clause: a standing long jump can span up to the current Strength score in feet; a running long jump uses that same base and retains Athlete's separate increase equal to the nonnegative current Strength modifier. The feat changes horizontal distance, not vertical clearance, a high jump, flight or safe landing. A legal check can still be needed for a hazardous takeoff or landing, and no success creates additional distance. These proposed standing/running distinctions and the10-foot approach need comparison with the complete movement source review before adoption.

currentPublic.name: Improved Climber

sourceObject.name: Improved Climber
sourceObject.description: You are an exceptional climber.
sourceObject.effect: You can climb on ceilings and overhangs, and you don't fall when you fail a climbing check by 4 or less.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Requires the actual Climber feat, ID climber. NEW: ceiling and overhang climbing is possible with actual usable grips, anchors or equipment sufficient for the current body's support; the feat removes the angle-only bar but supplies no adhesion to a featureless unsupported surface. Pay the ordinary climbing movement budget and make any real required check, including Climber's advantage when applicable. If that climb check fails by a final numerical deficit of1–4, you avoid the fall caused by that failed check. Remain at the last legally supported position, spend the movement/action/time already committed, and gain no progress through the failed segment. A natural-1 degree downgrade with deficit below5 still receives this narrow fall protection. A failed result with total meeting the DC due solely to a natural downgrade also avoids that check's fall under this NEW clarification. Deficit5+ receives no protection. The feat does not stop an unrelated shove, lost anchor, collapsing support, already ongoing fall or deliberate release. A retry needs a legally available new attempt under the climb task, without refunded movement.
workedCases: DC18, total14 fails by4: remain at the last supported place without gaining the failed traverse, and keep the spent movement cost. Total13 fails by5 and may fall normally.
A rope anchor breaks after a successful climb. That is a separate loss of support, so the feat's failed-check protection does not suspend the climber in air.

unchangedReviewedRecord.operationalRules:
## Inspiring Leader — General; Charisma13+

Speak for ten uninterrupted minutes. At the start, select up to your current PB **other** willing creatures within30ft. Snapshot your character level and actual signed Charisma modifier then. Each selected creature must remain in range, hear and understand you throughout. No replacements or retargeting during the speech.

On completion, each continuously eligible recipient receives `max(1, snapshotted level + actual CHA modifier)` temporary HP with default lifetime. Each recipient can receive one legal Inspiring-Leader-family offer per its own completed-long-rest epoch, shared across all speakers. An offer rejected by stronger/equal temporary HP still consumes the entitlement.

If one listener loses eligibility, only that listener misses the benefit. If the speaker becomes Incapacitated, cannot continue speaking or abandons the speech, the whole unfinished performance fails. Interrupted speeches spend no recipient entitlements and have no owner per-rest use; the speaker may begin again. Later changes in the speaker's statistics do not change this performance's snapshot. Temporary CHA below13 after acquisition does not disable ownership.

**NEW:** other-creature restriction, count, range/language/presence gates, amount, snapshots and family rest limit.

currentPublic.name: Inspiring Presence

sourceObject.name: Inspiring Presence
sourceObject.description: After a critical hit, Charisma 14+ inspires allies with the listed damage increase for 10 seconds.
sourceObject.effect: When you score a critical hit, allies within 30 feet who can see or hear you gain +1 to attack rolls until the start of your next turn.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules:
After your direct attack critically hits a meaningful hostile, allied creatures within30ft that can actually see or hear you at that instant gain+1 to their attack rolls through your next original regular start. NEW recipients are fixed at the trigger, with no continuing range/hearing tether; allies entering later do not gain the old inspiration. No common language is required. You may be your own recipient when you meet the same actual seeing-or-hearing predicate. Any genuine critical-if-hit result qualifies, not just natural20; automatic-hit wording without a critical does not. Same-feat overlapping records never add beyond+1, and independent expiry records remain. Another legitimate critical can renew eligible allies but cannot duplicate the number. Preserve older+5%damage/10seconds as history; current effect is+1attack, not damage.
SOURCE SCOPE CORRECTION: “allies” includes the feat owner unless the actual clause says “other.” The owner must still meet the same hearing/perception, range, willing-target and action/resource predicates. No second body, observer or extra action is created by self-eligibility. This sentence supersedes any narrower owner-exclusion in the submitted proposal, not the preserved original.
workedCases: A genuine personal critical fixes its actual eligible ally recipients, including the owner if they can see or hear the triggering presence. Each gains the single+1attack bonus until the owner’s next regular start; later entrants do not receive it retroactively.
Two inspiring owners grant one+1family layer to an ally; a later expiry can preserve that layer without making it+2.

sourceObject.description: Your presence strikes fear into others.
sourceObject.effect: You gain proficiency in Intimidation and can demoralize enemies in combat, causing them to have disadvantage on their next attack.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Gain Intimidation proficiency, not expertise if already proficient. NEW in combat spendBA to demoralize one hostile within30ft who perceives your audible or visible credible threat. Oppose your normal CHA Intimidation (STR only if an independently legal actual source permits that substitution) with targetWIS Insight. Higher wins, ties preserve state; no natural task shift. Success imposes disadvantage on its next attack roll before your next original regular start, consumed by that attack even if canceled or missed. currentPublic.name: Iron Will

sourceObject.name: Iron Will
sourceObject.description: Your willpower is unbreakable.
sourceObject.effect: +2 bonus to saves vs mind effects

currentPublic.operationalRules: Add 2 once to the actual saving throw against a mental effect meeting the shared proposed finite predicate. This can apply to an INT, WIS, CHA, CON or other save if the actual effect qualifies; it is not a blanket ability-based bonus. The same source cannot add twice when one effect both causes fear and deals psychic damage. No bonus applies to an opposed skill check, death save, ordinary concentration maintenance or an effect granting no save. NEW stacking completion: this distinct feat bonus can combine with Resilient Mind's independently applicable +1 Wisdom-save rider, subject to any explicit overriding source restriction; class-technique bonuses first obey their own strongest-only family. Preserve actual natural-save rules and any printed failure margin. The feat supplies no immunity, automatic success, new save, changed belief or agency override.

A Constitution concentration save caused by psychic damage is not itself the attack's mental-effect save; Iron Will does not add +2 merely from that causal history.

sourceObject.name: Jack of All Trades
sourceObject.description: Intelligence 12+ opens the listed two untrained skill slots.
sourceObject.effect: Choose two skills in which you lack proficiency. Add half your proficiency bonus, rounded down, to checks using those skills.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: At acquisition choose two distinct actual skills in which you lack proficiency. On an actual check using one of those skills, add floor(currentPB/2) while you remain unproficient. This is the proficiency contribution, not a bonus added to a different full/half/expert proficiency contribution on the same check; use one actually applicable strongest contribution. It does not count as trained proficiency, satisfy a proficient prerequisite, initialize a trade, modify tools, attacks, saves or an unskilled ability check. NEW: if you later gain proficiency in a chosen skill, use that full contribution and retain the original selection as inactive; there is no free retargeting or banked choice. If that separate proficiency is actually lost, this feat’s same half-PB contribution can resume. No new skill slots or free respec are created by its legacy wording.

sourceObject.description: You have a mind that can track time, direction, and detail.
sourceObject.effect: You always know which way is north, the number of hours left before sunrise or sunset, and can recall anything you have seen or heard within the past month.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Always know the direction designated as true north in the current region's established physical/map frame and the remaining elapsed hours to its actual next sunrise or sunset when that event exists. This requires no artificial navigation roll, but does not reveal passages, destinations or a safe route. NEW boundary: where no such direction/event is defined by actual setting evidence, record 'not defined here' or 'no scheduled event' rather than inventing a cosmological answer; confer on any real exception later. Accurately recall anything you actually perceived by sight or hearing within the past month, including sounds or marks you did not understand, without thereby translating them or learning concealed details. NEW: for this feat's memory window only, month means30elapsed24-hour days; this does not define the world's calendar. Recollection can reproduce the perceived sequence, but limited attention, obstructed senses and a deceptive illusion limit what was perceived. Explicit memory alteration follows its own effect. Numerical dawn-like recharge receipts are not evidence of sunrise. No soul, plane, alignment or celestial explanation is authored here.
workedCases: A rune seen clearly ten days ago can be recalled in its observed form, but an unread language remains untranslated. A hidden reverse side was never seen.
A place with no actual sunrise schedule receives no invented time-to-sunrise. An item that recharges at06:00 does not establish a sunrise at06:00.

currentPublic.name: Kill-Chain Adaptation

sourceObject.name: Kill-Chain Adaptation
sourceObject.description: Successful kills enhance your combat capabilities.
sourceObject.effect: After a melee kill, gain +10 ft movement and +1 to hit

currentPublic.operationalRules: NEW require Warrior4 and two actual Combat mutations equipped and active at the trigger. Once per numbered round, after your personal direct melee attack reduces an independent meaningful hostile from positiveHP to0, gain+10ft to each existing usable Speed mode and one+1 entitlement on your next melee attack roll, both ending at the end of your next future original regular turn. This intentionally selects the counterpart zeroHP trigger rather than requiring actual death; resolve floors/knockout/death replacements first. The trigger grants no attack or fullAction. Copies, owned companion damage, ongoing ticks, captives, harmless targets and recycled bodies do not qualify. Modes derived from another Speed include this bonus once, not twice; previously spent movement remains spent. The attack entitlement consumes on the next legal melee attack roll, hit or miss; a save-only melee effect does not consume it. Same-family new trigger may refresh an unexpired record under the once-round cap but never gives+20ft or queued+1s. It ends if required equipped or active mutation eligibility is lost, even before its deadline. Encounter transitions do not extend or refresh either benefit.
workedCases: A qualifying melee down adds10 towalk30, but moving30 earlier still leaves only10 ordinary movement after the newSpeed40.
A second down in the same round adds nothing. The next legal melee attack consumes+1 even if it misses.

currentPublic.name: Leadership

sourceObject.name: Leadership
sourceObject.description: You inspire others to follow you.
sourceObject.effect: You can recruit followers and hirelings more easily, and they are more loyal to you.

currentPublic.operationalRules: NEW finite recruitment/loyalty procedure: during a real recruitment effort, designate up to current PB actual willing prospective followers or hirelings. Spend one active hour interviewing and briefing them, agree on their actual jobs, pay, duration, risk, equipment and departure terms, and gain+2 on any legitimate Persuasion checks to secure those agreements. An automatic willing agreement needs no roll. The feat creates no candidate, free wage, stat block, level, binding, summoned unit or extra class companion. Keep at most PB current designated contracts receiving the feat's loyalty benefit; designate at agreement or at a new hour-long briefing, never retroactively during a morale event. While the employer honors the terms and the work remains within the agreed risk, a designated follower gains+2 on an actual loyalty/morale check whose purpose is deciding whether to abandon that agreement under pressure. This is not a bonus against every fear spell or a compulsion to stay; no roll is invented where the person's real decision is certain. Broken terms, unpaid wages or an unagreed suicidal demand remove this benefit until genuinely repaired and re-briefed. Actual transport, expedition caps, combat turns and command budgets continue to govern each recruited person. Dismissal ends designation without transferring any creature's property or earned wages.
workedCases: PB3 can designate three real hired people, each still requiring a valid contract and actual pay. The feat does not authorize a thirteenth expedition character against the owner's12-character cap.
A follower ordered into danger expressly excluded from their contract does not receive a loyalty check that forces compliance. The employer must negotiate a real change or accept refusal.

currentPublic.name: Librarian's Eye

sourceObject.name: Librarian's Eye
sourceObject.description: Intelligence 15+ supports recalling read text with the listed +5 recall bonus.
sourceObject.effect: You can accurately recall the substance of text you have read. Gain +2 on checks to quote, locate, or compare previously studied written material.
sourceObject.legacyEffect: Recall any read text with +5 recall bonus
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Accurately recall the substance of text you actually read and understood. NEW: record the material and relevant studied passage when its existence or scope is uncertain; the benefit preserves the text's content, not whether its claims are true. Verbatim quoting, locating a passage or comparing previously studied writings can still require an appropriate actual check; add +2 to that check. Recalling a straightforward understood summary needs no artificial roll solely to obtain a bonus. An unread cipher, unknown language, unseen page or remote revision is not previously studied content. Loss or alteration of memory by an explicit effect follows that effect. Knowing that a formula was discussed does not provide all missing formula instructions, research success, ownership rights or a prepared spell. The feat neither stores a perfect visual copy nor grants live remote access to the original.
workedCases: The holder remembers that a read ledger claimed a payment was made. They do not thereby know that the payment truly occurred.
A check to quote a specific sentence from a previously understood chapter gets +2. A sealed page never read gives no qualifying memory.

sourceObject.description: You have trained to master light armor.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Gain light-armor proficiency and shield proficiency, preserving both printed grants despite the feat's name. Recompute actual derived statistics without healing or refilling resources.

sourceObject.name: Lock Savant
sourceObject.description: Dexterity 15+ and Thievery 5+ provide the listed success increase on complex locks.
sourceObject.effect: Gain +2 on checks to open complex locks. A failed attempt does not trigger the lock’s trap unless you fail by 5 or more.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Add +2 on a lawful check to open a lock whose actual construction the Director identifies as complex before the attempt. Possess the necessary access and implements; the feat does not provide them or a universal permission to pick a magical seal. NEW: the source's protection applies only to a trap whose trigger is this lock-opening attempt failing. If the final total is less than DC by 5 or more, that protection does not apply and the trap's real trigger resolves. A natural-1 task downgrade without a five-point numerical deficit does not by itself remove this protection. Independent touch, proximity, damage, time, wrong-key or tampering triggers still operate at their own actual moments even on a success. A legally repeated failed attempt receives the same margin rule but spends its real time and remains exposed to all independent events; it cannot undo a previously triggered trap. Thievery's acquisition bridge is specified in the shared proposal.

currentPublic.operationalRules: When a creature within5ft actually casts a spell and you can perceive the casting event, you may spendReaction for one legal melee weapon attack against it. V/S or another actually perceptible magical cue can reveal casting; no automatic detection of fully imperceptible casting is granted.
