currentPublic.name: Magic Initiate (Cleric)

sourceObject.name: Magic Initiate (Cleric)
sourceObject.description: You have learned some cleric magic.
sourceObject.effect: You learn two cantrips and one 1st-level spell from the cleric spell list. You can cast the spell once per long rest.

currentPublic.operationalRules:
Choose two distinct cantrip identities and one rank1spell from this feat’s actual named choice pool. The preserved Cleric classAccess rows supply the actual rank0and rank1choice lists below; keep that row’s school/mode even when another class gives the same identity a different placement. Choices are permanent and grant only their chosen rank/mode. Use WIS as the feat casting ability. The two cantrips are repeatable with their actual card actions and cadence; the one ranked spell has one charge per beneficial Long Rest. Apply the full proposed feat casting route: actual components and independent costs remain, no normal rankRPprice, no new RPpool/class levels/preparation, shared Dissonance/Refrain and rank1strain block, and no generic scaling. Current reviewed payload status is separate from grant eligibility; an unfinished chosen payload cannot be activated. A qualifying cantrip with its own character-wide Long-Rest limit retains that limit despite the word cantrip.

NEW duplicate policy across the general Magic Initiate record and the six named records: one selected curriculum label per character in this family; the general feat can supply that same named grant but cannot be taken alongside its named version to double the same curriculum. Distinct curricula are separate feat selections and may coexist; they grant no multiclass level. A repeated spell name can have distinct source entitlements, but its own genuine character-wide caps and one shared same-name strain history remain. Record duplicates rather than granting replacement spells automatically. This family decision must be confirmed alongside GC’s general Magic Initiate source. A separate ordinary class may cast a feat-learned identity only after that class independently meets its actual learning/preparation/access requirements; the feat alone does not make it a free known spell on every paid route.
workedCases: A character with no Cleric class level spends a genuine feat selection on this route and makes the three legal choices. It uses WIS and total PB for those spell attacks/saves but gains no Cleric class card, RPpool or automatic Extra Attack.

The ranked charge is spent at legal cast commitment even if countered. A chosen cantrip that independently costs1RP still needs a real payable RPpool; neither the charge route nor cantrip label manufactures one.

sourceObject.name: Mana Burn
sourceObject.description: Intelligence-trained offensive spellwork carries the feat's listed drain against an enemy's RP.
sourceObject.effect: When a creature fails a save against your damaging spell, it loses 1 RP if it has an RP pool. A creature can lose RP this way only once per round.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: After a creature fails an actual save against your personally cast damaging spell, remove 1 from its realRPpool, minimum 0. NEW damaging means that same spell application has a native damage component governed by that save; full prevention/immunity may leave 0 damage without negating the failed-save trigger. A repeat save solely ending nondamaging control after earlier damage does not qualify. Commit one recipient-wide Mana Burn entitlement per numbered round across all owners/casts on the first qualifying failure with anRPpool, even at RP 0; no further loss that round. Resolve native damage and immediate survival replacements first, then loss if the target still exists as a living resource holder. No transfer to you, charge/RC/slot substitution, maximum reduction or loss from RP-less creatures. Copies, echoes and reflected packets cannot create a fresh proc.
workedCases: Two casters trigger Mana Burn against the same RP 4 foe this round: total loss is 1, leaving 3.
A target immune to the damage can still lose 1 RP after failing the associated save; an RP-less monster loses nothing.

currentPublic.name: Master Tracker

sourceObject.name: Master Tracker
sourceObject.description: Survival 4+ and Wisdom 13+ support the listed tracking with +10 accuracy.
sourceObject.effect: Gain +2 on Survival checks to track. You can track at a normal travel pace and identify the approximate number, size, and age of tracks on a successful check.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Add +2 on Survival checks whose actual purpose is tracking. Follow existing, perceivable tracks at the adopted normal travel pace and, on an actual successful tracking check, identify the approximate count, size and age of the tracks to the precision the evidence supports. NEW: use Wisdom (Survival) for following and reading tracks unless an actual task expressly calls for another ability. Record a range or uncertainty rather than fabricate an exact census from poor evidence. The normal-pace permission changes only the tracking activity and does not remove travel hazards, actual visibility limits, route access, cargo constraints or stealth penalties. No tracks, obliterated tracks or an unrelated map cannot become usable tracks solely because the feat is owned. Preserve `skill_feats1_master_tracker` as an alias of `master_tracker`; it adds no second acquisition or +2.
workedCases: Success may reveal roughly three Medium walkers who passed within the last hour. Intermixed prints may justify a count range rather than an exact identity.
A save containing both the current ID and its compatibility alias represents one feat and one +2 contribution, never +4.

currentPublic.name: Medium Armor Master

sourceObject.name: Medium Armor Master
sourceObject.description: You have mastered medium armor.
sourceObject.effect: Wearing medium armor doesn't impose disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks and you can add 3 to AC instead of 2 if you have a Dexterity of 16 or higher.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Require medium-armor proficiency at acquisition. While wearing an actual medium suit, remove only that suit's Stealth-disadvantage cause; other remaining causes still combine normally with advantage. When the selected operative AC formula is that medium suit's formula and your current Dexterity score is at least 16, raise its Dexterity contribution cap from 2 to 3. Use the actual Dexterity modifier, including any penalty, capped at 3; this is not a flat +3 added to AC. If Dexterity falls below 16, use the ordinary cap of 2. A shield's legal bonus remains separate, and another chosen unarmored/natural formula gains nothing from this medium-suit modification. NEW: a Broken or otherwise nonbeneficial suit supplies no positive AC formula benefit, although removing that suit's Stealth-disadvantage cause still applies while it is physically worn. Other properties, weight, Strength limits and actual fit remain.
workedCases: A medium suit with base AC 14 and DEX 16 contributes 14+3=17 before a real shield. DEX 14 uses 14+2=16.
Removing the suit's Stealth disadvantage does not remove an unrelated Exhaustion disadvantage or grant automatic Hidden.

currentPublic.name: Merchant’s Guile

sourceObject.name: Merchant’s Guile
sourceObject.description: Charisma 13+ supports the feat's listed ten-percent improvement to trade prices.
sourceObject.effect: When buying or selling ordinary goods, improve the final negotiated price by up to 10 percent after a successful Persuasion, Deception, or relevant Profession check. This cannot override monopolies or fixed guild tariffs.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Use with an actual willing transaction in ordinary mundane goods, a finite buyer/seller and a quoted quantity. Exclude artifacts, magic-item effects, labor/services, taxes, guild tariffs and monopolies unless their own exact rule expressly admits ordinary negotiation. NEW procedure: before the check the provider states its ordinary quote, whether the deal is negotiable, the supported improvement ceiling0–10%, the relevant approach and a concrete price-persuasion DC, default15 for an ordinary receptive negotiation. Spend10actual minutes and make CHA/Persuasion for honest bargaining, CHA/Deception for an actual plausible misrepresentation, or an actually applicable established Profession credential with its ordinary ability; this does not create a new Profession skill. Success or Critical Success gives the agreed ceiling, default10% if a negotiable ordinary deal has no smaller stated ceiling; Failure/Critical Failure gives no feat discount and preserves the source’s actual deception consequences. The result changes the final otherwise-negotiated purchase by×(1-ceiling) or sale by×(1+ceiling), before final copper rounding, with no double count of the same concession. NEW same concession family: multiple owners/repeated checks cannot compound this feat or claim another10% on the same deal. A change of speaker or splitting one order does not reset unchanged-state negotiation. Keep the actual provider’s predeclared floor/ceiling and refusal; no roll creates stock, consent or guaranteed profit. Reconcile the final58-question social/settlement verdict before adoption.
workedCases: A real100gp ordinary sale quote with an agreed10% ceiling becomes110gp after a successful check. Two feat owners cannot turn that same negotiated deal into121gp.

A fixed guild tariff remains fixed. A separately willing ordinary seller offering only a3% concession gives3% on success, with the ceiling disclosed before work; the feat does not secretly convert success into a different costly-agreement outcome.

currentPublic.name: Metamagic Adept

sourceObject.name: Metamagic Adept
sourceObject.description: You have learned to modify your spells in subtle ways.
sourceObject.effect: Learn 2 metamagic options, gain 2 sorcery points

currentPublic.operationalRules:
Keep personal spellcasting and total character level4. NEW grant a separate pool of two feat sorcery points, maximum2, initially full and restored to2only by a beneficial Long Rest. There is no RP/RC/HP/charge exchange, class-resource conversion, overcap or refill from ordinary spell refunds. At acquisition permanently choose two distinct modes from the finite three-mode menu below, based explicitly on the actual Mage Metaspell Access card; this does not acquire that Mage card or its Long-Rest use.

Reach: spend1point when committing a personal spell cast to add30feet to its finite positive numeric casting range. Self,Touch,unlimited and a separate effect/command radius do not gain range. Widen: spend1point at commitment to add5feet to one circular/spherical area radius or one cone length of that actual spell; choose the one eligible dimension in advance, not all independent areas/parameters. It does not create an area on a single-target spell. Sculpt: spend1point at commitment to choose up to max(1,actual casting ability modifier) eligible creatures in that spell’s initial area; they automatically succeed on its initial save and take no damage if that success would normally halve damage. Their later saves/ticks and nondamage successful-save consequences follow the original spell; there is no permanent friendly-fire immunity.

NEW one metamagic mode total per cast across this feat and Mage Metaspell Access; declare which actual source pays. You cannot use two points for two modes or duplicate a class mode on the same cast. Other separately applicable feats keep their exact scopes. Spell Sniper doubles the printed numeric range first, then Reach adds30; it does not double Reach’s30. The chosen mode adds no spell rank, RPdiscount, Action, concentration slot or second cast. Commit the point with the legal spell; a later miss, save, counter or interruption refunds neither. Illegal mode/target declarations spend nothing. The spell still needs all its own resources, components and access.
workedCases: A caster with Reach and Sculpt spends1point to extend a60-foot ranged spell to90feet. If Spell Sniper legally applies too, range is150feet:120from doubled printed range plus30.
After spending its second point, the caster cannot convertRPinto more sorcery points. Having the Mage card’s own use does not allow an additional mode on a cast already modified through this feat.

sourceObject.name: Mirror Cast
sourceObject.description: Intelligence 16+ permits the feat's listed once-per-day spell cast from a reflection.
sourceObject.effect: Once per long rest, cast a spell as though originating from a reflective surface you can see within 60 feet. Range and line of effect are measured from that surface.
sourceObject.legacyEffect: Cast spell from reflection (once per day)
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Once LR at cast declaration choose a real reflective surface you can see within 60 ft of your actual body. NEW require an unobstructed line of effect from you to that surface, at least hand-sized, sufficiently exposed to form a recognizable reflection; a drawn picture of a mirror is insufficient. Choose an unoccupied origin point immediately at its visible face. Measure spell range/line of effect and area orientation from that point; you still must personally perceive targets where the spell requires it, receiving no remote senses. Self-area/cone origins can relocate, but a Self-only body buff still affects you and Touch spells still require actual touch; no remote grasp. Hostile-held surfaces may serve if visibly legal; no possession or movement of the object. Commit ordinary costs/components/feat use at your body, preserving its interruption window. The origin is snapshotted for immediate resolution; destruction before resolution fails the changed origin with no refund. Ongoing created areas retain their actual fixed/moving rules and deadlines; the mirror is neither a second caster nor an unprinted tether.
workedCases: A cone can originate at a visible mirror 40 ft away and point along a chosen legal direction.
An unseen creature behind the mirror gains no free visibility; a Touch heal cannot cross 40 ft through it.

currentPublic.name: Mounted Combatant

sourceObject.name: Mounted Combatant
sourceObject.description: You are a dangerous foe to face while mounted.
sourceObject.effect: You have advantage on melee attack rolls against unmounted creatures smaller than your mount.

currentPublic.operationalRules:
While you are actually legally mounted, gain advantage on your melee attack rolls against creatures that are unmounted and smaller than the actual ridden mount at resolution. Include melee weapon, natural, unarmed and actual melee spell attacks; no ranged or save-only effect. Use real mount/target sizes, not rider size, names or desired posture. Other disadvantage cancels normally. This grants no mount, proficiency/control, target redirection, mount save evasion, immunity, extra action or shared turn. Cavalry's broader advantage is separate, but two sources still roll only two dice. The completed EX58 transport rules govern actual mounting, movement, custody and eligibility.
NEW explicit EX58 interface: retain one real creature identity and one current control/phase record. Riding, bonding or transferring custody does not clone a turn, movement budget, Reaction, attack allowance, body or resource pool. An attached companion acts in its source-defined phase after the owner’s regular turn; a controlled mount uses EX58’s actual mounted-phase procedure. A body fitting both roles elects one compatible route before that round’s work, preserves all already-spent allowances and cannot switch routes to gain a second phase. Its actual load, tack, rider geometry, mounting/dismounting cost and ordinary independent temperament remain. One shared Bonus Action command and one offensive companion action per owner per numbered round apply where those source engines impose them. This feat supplies no blanket override of a specific engine’s attack or no-resource restrictions.

currentPublic.name: Negotiator

sourceObject.name: Negotiator
sourceObject.description: You excel at making deals.
sourceObject.effect: You can negotiate better prices for goods and services, and you have advantage on Persuasion checks during negotiations.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Gain advantage on actual Persuasion checks during negotiations for real goods or services. NEW: before the check, establish the seller/buyer's available stock, normal quote, attainable concession, payment and conditions. A successful check secures that announced better quote or term; no universal percentage discount or guaranteed buyer is created. A concession can be a lower price, improved payment schedule, delivery, included fitting or a better actual sale offer, with its exact value set before rolling. The counterpart must have authority and willingness to consider it. Failed unchanged negotiations cannot be repeated by restating the same bargain or swapping speakers without a materially changed offer or evidence. Distinct standing, sponsor and service benefits use their own actual clauses; advantage does not stack. Different purchase and resale quotes remain separate, and this feat never establishes a same-price repurchase promise or circular money source. Record the final agreement and any taxes/fees through the actual settlement procedure.
workedCases: A merchant offers a possible reduction from50gp to45gp on success. A successful advantaged check secures45gp under the announced terms; it does not also apply another unprinted10% discount.
Buying for45gp does not force any buyer to repurchase for50gp. A later actual resale uses that buyer's own stock, demand and quote.

sourceObject.name: Nightfang Training
sourceObject.description: Racial feat tied to Umbrin heritage.
sourceObject.effect: You gain +10% damage and +2 stealth in total darkness.

currentPublic.operationalRules:
Require actual Umbrin heritage. While your actual occupied space is in total darkness, gain+2 to actualDEXStealth checks and add floor(native damage/10) to each eligible personal direct attack/spell damage event. NEW your whole occupied footprint must be dark, not dim or partly illuminated; determine this independently from darkvision, which changes perception rather than illumination. It grants no ability to see targets, Hide automatically or ignore your actual Sunlight Sensitivity. Damage bonus uses the already proposed common pre-percentage base after native critical-dice adjustment and native ordinary ability modifier, before other feat/class riders, saving-throw reduction and defenses; allocate increment across native typed components by proportional largest remainder with stable ties. Count direct initial attacks/spell resolutions, not copies, companion attacks, transfers or later ongoing ticks; one genuine shared area roll receives its one native increment before each recipient's saving-throw reduction and defenses. No new attack/damage event or added damage type. Check darkness at the attack/spell's actual damage resolution and at the Stealth check; a light-generating effect can remove eligibility before damage. Distinct percentage sources do not compound and the flatStealth bonus never grants a proficiency credential.
NEW damage-stage correction: calculate floor(10% of the eligible initial native personally owned attack/spell packet after native critical adjustment but before saving-throw reduction and defenses). Do not calculate it after the save, include external riders/percentages, or apply it to copied/companion results. Add distinct percentage feat riders without compounding under FS-04.
workedCases: A qualifying native19damage packet adds1 before defenses; later darkness-independent poison ticks do not inherit the feat bonus.
Darkvision lets the Umbrin perceive a dark square but does not turn it bright. A square actually lit dimly no longer qualifies.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Once LR at damaging spell declaration, add one existing native damage die per actual spell rank to one immediate native packet under the shared added-die rule. NEW choose this active rule over legacy 25%. Commit use with the cast. After its immediate attempted resolution, including a miss, all saves or Counterspell, take 2×rank force backlash as one self-damage event. This damage cannot be reduced or redirected; NEW it does pass through real temp HP before normal HP, unlike the explicitly proposed normal HP-funded blood costs. Resolve ordinary Wound/death/concentration consequences and no incidental reflection/resource/lifesteal triggers from this self-authored cost. It requires noHPprepayment and can kill the caster. Rank 0 legally adds 0 dice and 0 damage but still spends the use if chosen. Flat-only/no-native-die spells are ineligible.

sourceObject.name: Overrun
sourceObject.description: With Strength 15+, you press through movement by pushing enemies aside as the feat lists.
sourceObject.effect: When you Dash, you may move through spaces occupied by creatures no more than one size larger. Each may make a Strength save against DC 8 + proficiency bonus + Strength modifier or be pushed 5 feet aside.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: When you legally take Dash, activate Overrun for that turn's subsequent ordinary movement; Dash supplies its normal increased cap, not a second separate movement grant. You may attempt passage through actual creatures at most one size larger, allied or hostile. NEW each distinct creature may be challenged once that turn, with no duplicate attempt from extra Dashes. Before entering its first occupied space, it makes STR save DC8+PB+your STR; a willing ally may elect failure as this feat's explicit exception. On failure push it5ft to a legal adjacent side destination you choose that clears the necessary passage. Success, anchoring, or no legal clearing destination blocks this special passage; remain outside and spend the attempted first entry step's ordinary cost. Do not start without enough budget for a complete legal path/end. The feat does not suppress opportunity attacks. A creature already passable under ordinary size rules can instead be crossed normally without invoking the feature. It grants no Prone, damage or ability to remain in occupied space.
workedCases: A Medium runner Dashes and a Large guard fails; a legal5ft side space clears the route, so the runner proceeds using ordinary cost.
A guard fills a narrow passage with no side destination. Failure alone cannot teleport it through the wall; Overrun passage stays blocked.

originalObject.effect: When you Dash, you may move through spaces occupied by creatures no more than one size larger. Each may make a Strength save against DC 8 + proficiency bonus + Strength modifier or be pushed 5 feet aside.
originalObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

You may attempt passage through actual creatures at most one size larger, allied or hostile. NEW each distinct creature may be challenged once that turn, with no duplicate attempt from extra Dashes. Before entering its first occupied space, it makes STR save DC8+PB+your STR; a willing ally may elect failure as this feat's explicit exception. On failure push it5ft to a legal adjacent side destination you choose that clears the necessary passage. currentPublic.name: Pathfinder

sourceObject.name: Pathfinder
sourceObject.description: You can navigate any terrain.
sourceObject.effect: You and your party can move at normal speed while tracking, and difficult terrain doesn't slow your group's travel.

currentPublic.operationalRules: While you actively lead one physically coordinated traveling party, the party may track at its actual normal travel pace and ignore ordinary difficult terrain's reduction of strategic travel rate. NEW: party members must remain on the led route and able to follow your current directions directly or through their actual communications chain; separated scouts and a different caravan receive no remote benefit. Use the normal rate of the actual slowest participating body/vehicle, with actual capacity, access and work/rest limits. A mount or wagon can benefit only on a route it can physically traverse; the feat supplies neither a road through an impassable gap nor a swim/fly/climb mode. Severe weather, visibility, moving currents, climbing tasks, hazards, loading and other independent delays still apply. This changes the difficult-terrain travel-rate factor and tracking activity, not tactical difficult-terrain movement costs, combat Speed, forced-march rules or resource consumption. If leadership/coordination ends, subsequent travel uses ordinary rates; already elapsed time is not recalculated.
workedCases: A coordinated party with a slower laden wagon uses that wagon's actual normal route rate while ignoring the ordinary rough-ground slowdown. The feat cannot make the wagon cross a path narrower than its body.
A scout who leaves the coordinated route loses the group benefit for their separate travel. During combat, ordinary difficult-terrain costs still apply.

currentPublic.name: Piercer

sourceObject.name: Piercer
sourceObject.description: You are adept at dealing piercing damage.
sourceObject.effect: When you hit with a piercing weapon, you can reroll one damage die and critical hits add an extra damage die.

currentPublic.operationalRules: NEW once per turn, after rolling damage for a personal hit with a weapon whose native type includes piercing, you may reroll one actual piercing base-weapon die and must keep its new face. Choose from native weapon dice including critical copies and expressly additional weapon dice, not poison/Smite/spell rider dice. One Piercer reroll per event/turn; no repeated loop. Separately, every critical hit with that piercing weapon adds one additional die of its actual base weapon expression after ordinary critical doubling; this critical-specific die is not doubled again. NEW if Savage Attacker also applies, resolve its whole-pool choice first, then Piercer on one die of the kept pool; no return to a discarded pool. All source-specific reroll limits remain.

sourceObject.description: Dexterity 14+ supports a ranged attack into melee without the feat's listed penalty.
sourceObject.effect: Your ranged attacks ignore the disadvantage normally imposed by an ally being adjacent to the target.
sourceObject.legacyEffect: No penalty for ranged into melee
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: The current combat guide imposes no general disadvantage just because an ally is adjacent to the target; retain that printed historical removal as a compatibility clause if a specifically enabled source ever supplies it. NEW useful completion for this candidate: your ranged weapon or ranged spell attack ignores half cover when that half cover is supplied solely by one or more allied creature bodies in the shot's actual path. It ignores neither terrain cover, three-quarters/total cover, hostile-body cover, nearby-hostile disadvantage, nor long-range disadvantage. Compute remaining actual cover normally after disregarding those allied bodies; never lower a real wall's cover. This does not make firing through solid or untargetable positions legal and does not acquire a class Sharpshooter feature.

sourceObject.description: At level 6, casting grants the listed +10% AC for 5 seconds.

currentPublic.operationalRules: At character level 6, after a completed personal ranked cast gain+1 AC until your next future regular start. NEW select active+1/regular-start over preserved 10%/5 seconds. Ready release does not grant again. Incapacity does not itself end this nonconcentration buff; ordinary expiry/source-suppression does. No additional armor, resistance, spell use or cast trigger from copies.

currentPublic.name: Punishing Blow

sourceObject.name: Punishing Blow
sourceObject.description: Strength 13+ supports the listed +10% bonus against a stunned enemy.
sourceObject.effect: Once per turn, deal additional damage equal to your proficiency bonus to a stunned or prone enemy.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Once per turn, on one of your own direct attacks that hits a genuine enemy already Stunned or Prone immediately before damage, add your current PB as a flat damage component of that hit's native type. Choose one native type if the attack has several; if it deals no native damage, no additional damage is created. NEW all actual attack types qualify, including spell, natural and unarmed, because source says deal additional damage without weapon restriction. No application from a save-only effect, periodic tick, transfer, copy or rider that does not itself attack. The same hit cannot first inflict Prone/Stunned and retroactively qualify. The bonus is part of the hit before defenses, cannot double on a critical, and applies once across multi-type components.
workedCases: PB4 adds4 to a critical against a creature already Prone; it does not become8.
Bull Rush knocks the standing target Prone after damage. That same attack does not receive Punishing Blow retroactively.

currentPublic.name: Quick Recovery

sourceObject.name: Quick Recovery
sourceObject.description: Constitution 12+ supports the listed +50% HP regeneration outside combat.
sourceObject.effect: When you spend Hit Dice during a short rest, add your proficiency bonus to the total hit points restored.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Preserve the current effect: when you legally spend one or more Hit Dice during a completed short-rest recovery procedure, add your current PB once to the total ordinary HP-healing amount for that rest. NEW: commit this single Quick-Recovery-family addition with the first actual Hit Die healing event of that rest; further installments or extra dice in the same rest do not add it again. Zero spent Hit Dice yields no feat addition. Add PB before the ordinary healing reductions, prohibitions and capacity/Critical caps; it is not a promise of PB actual HP restored. The entitlement is spent even if that first event is blocked or entirely excess, and a separate owned converter still needs its own actual rules. Wounds affect recovered Hit Dice under their existing procedure, not a second fee on this bonus. The description/legacy +50-percent out-of-combat regeneration remains preserved but inactive. No free recurring regeneration, extra rest reward or new Hit Dice is created.

currentPublic.name: Quick Ritualist

sourceObject.name: Quick Ritualist
sourceObject.description: Wisdom 14+ supports halving the listed ritual casting time.
sourceObject.effect: Halve the additional casting time required to cast a spell as a ritual, to a minimum of 5 minutes.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules:
For a spell you can actually cast through a legal ritual route, halve only the route’s additional ritual time, with resulting additional time at least 5 minutes; retain the base printed casting time in full. NEW measure the result in elapsed seconds and round up to the next whole second so fractions never shorten a required interval. An original 10 minute addition becomes 5 minutes, not half the whole cast. An original shorter addition is not increased: use min(original additional time, max(300, ceil(original/2))). This explicit non-worsening interpretation preserves the minimum for reductions without penalizing a preexisting faster route. Components, formula/repertoire, costs, concentration, helpers and interruptions remain. It grants no Ritual tag or access; the separate proposed Ritual Caster overlay needs its own approval. Apply this additional-time change before any separately legal group active-time adjustment, whose minimum rule remains.
NEW common ritual arithmetic: let B be the spell’s actual base casting labor and A its separately required added ritual labor, in whole seconds. Quick Ritualist changes A to min(A,max(300,ceil(A/2))), leaving B unchanged. This never lengthens an already shorter source procedure. Literal source-required elapsed waiting is not active labor to halve.
workedCases: For a rank1 ritual with base Action6seconds plus600seconds added ritual labor, Quick Ritualist gives6+300=306seconds. It does not halve the base casting Action.
With Ritual Channeler as well,ceil(306×0.75)=230 would breach the6+300floor, so the result remains306seconds. No helper creates another spell, omitted component or concentration slot.

currentPublic.name: Ranger Training

sourceObject.name: Ranger Training
sourceObject.description: You have learned wilderness survival techniques.
sourceObject.effect: You gain proficiency in Survival and Nature, and you can hide even when only lightly obscured by natural phenomena.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Gain proficiency in Survival and Nature. Existing proficiency gives no Expertise under the proposed fixed-grant rule. You may attempt to Hide while only lightly obscured by actual natural phenomena, such as naturally occurring foliage, rainfall, falling snow, fog or blowing dust that genuinely interferes with the observer's view. NEW: this is an express eligibility exception to the ordinary clear-sight bar only while that qualifying partial obscurity exists; it permits a real Hide attempt against each affected observer, not automatic Hidden. Use normal Stealth, observer-specific passive DC, sound, other senses and revealing-event rules. A fully clear view or an observer unaffected by that natural obscurity gains no new bar to seeing you. Ordinary darkness and magical concealment use their own source permissions; merely naming a magical effect 'natural' does not qualify it here. The feat grants no Ranger class level, spells, companion, tracking expertise or movement benefit.
workedCases: Actual rain lightly obscures a character from one observer, permitting a Hide attempt. The character still rolls Stealth and can fail to become Hidden from that observer.
A creature using an unaffected sense or a clear angle does not lose the character's position solely because another observer's view is obscured.

currentPublic.name: Reckless Swing

sourceObject.name: Reckless Swing
sourceObject.description: Strength 15+ supports the listed +50% damage with -10% defense.
sourceObject.effect: Before making a melee weapon attack, choose to attack recklessly. Gain advantage on the attack and add one weapon damage die on a hit; attacks against you have advantage until the start of your next turn.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Before any melee weapon attack roll, you may declare Reckless Swing. That one attack gains advantage and adds one base weapon damage die if it hits; critical doubles that additional attack die. Regardless of hit, miss or advantage cancellation, all attacks against you have advantage through your next original regular start. Repeated declarations on separately legal attacks can each supply their one die but do not stack attacker advantage or create attacks; overlapping vulnerability records retain the same next-start deadline. This is not a rage and has no resistance or ability-score substitution. Spell, thrown ranged and unarmed attacks do not qualify; actual natural weapon melee attacks do. Ordinary costs, conditions and damage-source restrictions remain.
workedCases: A longsword1d8 attack gains1d8; if critical, roll4d8 plus flat modifiers.
You attack an unseen target: advantage and disadvantage cancel, but the extra die on a hit and attacks-against advantage still apply.

sourceObject.name: Resilient
sourceObject.description: Choose one ability score. You gain the following benefits:
sourceObject.effect: Increase the chosen ability score by 1, gain proficiency in saving throws using the chosen ability

currentPublic.operationalRules: Choose one of STR, DEX, CON, INT, WIS or CHA. Increase that score by 1, normally no higher than 20, and gain proficiency in saving throws using that same ability. NEW repeatability: a later actual feat opportunity can select a different ability, but cannot select the same ability again through this feat. Check the score ceiling for each selection. Apply the actual save ability only when that save is made, including other legitimate modifiers; proficiency is not a bonus to every save. Recompute derived statistics and the CON/maximum-HP records where relevant without ordinary healing or resource refills.

sourceObject.name: Riposte
sourceObject.description: You can quickly counterattack after successfully defending.
sourceObject.effect: Free attack after dodge/parry

currentPublic.operationalRules: NEW acquisition bridge: the legacy Agility15 means DEX15 for this feat only; Melee Proficiency means actual proficiency with at least one melee weapon. sourceObject.description: You have learned to cast spells as rituals.
sourceObject.effect: You can cast spells with the ritual tag without expending ranked-spell recoverys, but it takes 10 minutes longer.

currentPublic.operationalRules:
Keep INT13orWIS13; choose one qualifying ability permanently as this feat’s casting ability. The current848ordinary-card scan finds no explicit Ritual tag in their preserved Core-source tag arrays; neither a familiar external spell name nor a class procedure called ritual proves such a tag. NEW proposed Ritual-tag overlay below explicitly supplies seven existing reviewed rank1payload placements: Detect Magic,Identify,Comprehend Languages,Alarm,Unseen Servant,Find Familiar andIllusory Script, each using its exact Wizard source placement solely to fix rank/school/effect provenance. This conference adopts these seven NEW tags in a separate feat/Wizard-ritual interface overlay, leaving all original spell objects and class acquisition/status labels unchanged. The existing Wizard Ritual Casting feature can use the tags only with its own actual level, known-book spell, preparation, component, time and encounter predicates. It changes neither those spell effects nor their ordinary class membership.

NEW feat learning route: with an actual complete legitimate formula/text or a willing qualified teacher who genuinely knows the exact ritual, spend8active hours per rank and10gp per rank of real practice/writing materials to record it in your actual usable ritual book. Rank0, if ever separately admitted, uses one rank for this learning cost. A suitable blank book, ink/tools, language access and actual instructor/facility costs remain real. Study uses completed15-minute phases under the language/research clock; it is spell learning/copying, not ordinary research for Diligent Researcher’s discount. There is no random completion roll, free formula, duplicate-learning benefit or tradeXP. The feat grants no free starting ritual or physical book. Its maximum recorded/cast ritual rank is min(9,floor((total character level+1)/2)); this explicit feat-only gate grants no class advancement. The present proposed tag set has only rank1entries, and future entries need their own exact review.

To cast a legitimately learned recorded ritual, use its actual book and all components, spend its ordinary casting time plus ten actual minutes of uninterrupted active casting, and meet its complete targets/action-trigger rules. This route cannot complete during an encounter; interruption ends the attempt with real time and committed consumables spent. NEW maintain concentration during the long casting procedure, ending incompatible prior concentration at commitment; at resolution continue only the resulting spell’s own concentration if any. Do not choose a Reaction-triggered spell and manufacture its trigger through slow preparation. Ordinary rankRPprice and price-only surcharge are0; an expressly printed consumedRPconversion or other independent cost still applies and needs an actual pool. No ordinary Dissonance generation or vent, no Refrain addition/reset or history alteration, and no resource recovery from merely completing the casting time; a spell’s explicitly bounded actual effect remains its own effect. This follows the intended ordinary ritual separation rather than creating an at-will strain reset. Actual Counterspell eligibility, one-attempt-per-pending-cast guards, components and range apply. Source-specific per-rest limits remain. The adopted Quick Ritualist and Ritual Channeler rules may reduce actual ritual labor only as specified in this conference; neither changes output, eligibility or independent costs.

The source’s separate eight-hour-per-rank learning and ten-gp-per-rank transcription procedure is not itself a ritual cast or generic research discount.

sourceObject.description: Intelligence 14+ supports the listed 25% faster group rituals.
sourceObject.effect: When participating in a group ritual, reduce its required active casting time by 25 percent and count as two ordinary assistants.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules:
NEW a group ritual is one actual legally available ritual spell with a designated lead and at least one physically present willing assistant continuously performing that same ritual’s active work; it is not simultaneous crafting, travel or independent casts. Use the exact source’s assistant qualifications/cap. If it supplies none, the proposed default assistant must know that ritual or have proficiency in the lead’s actual relevant Arcana/Religion/Nature skill; count at most two ordinary assistant contributions, with no numeric roll bonus when the source has no assistant benefit. This feat-holder contributes as two ordinary assistants within that cap, never as two leads or two physical bodies for a separate location requirement. One or more holders reduce the group’s total active casting time once by 25%, rounding up seconds; passive waiting is unchanged. Apply after Quick Ritualist’s additional-time reduction, but never reduce that remaining additional ritual portion below 5 minutes unless it was already shorter. Source-required simultaneous people, costs, lead concentration, interruptions and minimum times remain. No multiplicative 25%stack or free spell/resource. NEW the double-assistant contribution applies only while actually serving as an assistant. A lead who owns this feat can supply the time reduction but cannot simultaneously count as two assistants; one person never performs both assigned jobs at once.

currentPublic.name: Rogue’s Escape

sourceObject.name: Rogue’s Escape
sourceObject.description: Dexterity 15+ at level 7 supports the listed one automatic Escape Artist success each day.
sourceObject.effect: Once per long rest, when restrained or grappled, you may automatically succeed on the check or save to escape.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Once per completed long rest, while actually Grappled or Restrained, you may declare automatic success in place of one check or save that the holding effect actually permits to escape. NEW: declare and spend the use immediately before rolling, after choosing the legal escape action and paying its normal action or other cost. This supplies ordinary Success, not Critical Success or a natural 20. For an opposed escape, it wins that one permitted escape contest. Resolve the printed successful escape outcome for the selected holding effect; independent grapples/restraints remain unless that source's single check ends them together. No-check prisons, an inaccessible release mechanism, unconscious action restrictions or a feature forbidding an escape attempt are not bypassed. The feat changes no location by itself and grants neither movement nor teleportation. The spent use is not refunded because another restraint still holds you.
workedCases: Spend an Action and the feat use on the one grapple's allowed Athletics/Acrobatics escape; it succeeds, but a separate magical restraint requiring its own save remains.
A sealed stone cell with no Grappled/Restrained escape check provides no eligible activation and spends no feat use.

currentPublic.name: Runic Scholar

sourceObject.name: Runic Scholar
sourceObject.description: Arcana 5+ and Intelligence 14+ support the listed instant identification of magical symbols.
sourceObject.effect: After studying a magical symbol for 1 minute, identify its school, activation method, and whether it is harmful without triggering it, unless it is protected by mythic concealment.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Study one actual magical symbol for one continuous minute with sufficient direct perception of its relevant marks. NEW: passive visual or equivalent noncontact examination by this procedure is not itself treated as activating that symbol, including a trigger based solely on this feat's act of looking or recognizing. It does not suppress a trigger already satisfied by approach, touch, entering a ward, speech, a third party or elapsed time; those can interrupt or harm the scholar normally. Do not touch, speak an activation or cross a ward as a free part of study. At completion learn the actual school, activation method and whether activation is harmful. If the source has no school, report that instead of inventing one. An explicit mythic concealment blocks this information and is not dispelled. This is recognition of magical operation, not translation of arbitrary surrounding writing; ordinary language rules still govern quoted words and other text. Identification grants no control, disarming, copied spell or hidden formula.
workedCases: Studying a gaze-activated rune by this exact procedure does not activate it solely through that studying gaze. Crossing its separately specified threshold before the minute ends still triggers it.
A time-triggered mark activates at its deadline during the minute; the feat does not pause the deadline or retroactively finish the study.

sourceObject.name: Runic Shield
sourceObject.description: Wisdom 14+ supports the listed absorption of the first 50 spell damage per combat.
sourceObject.effect: At the start of combat, gain a runic ward with 15 hit points. The ward absorbs spell damage first and vanishes when depleted. It refreshes after a short rest.
sourceObject.legacyEffect: Absorbs first 50 spell damage per combat
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: NEW select 15 ward HP over preserved 50. The feat has one armed grant per beneficial SR/LR; acquisition arms it. At the first real encounter start after arming, automatically create one personal runic ward with 15 points and spend that entitlement, even if surprised/incapacitated; a dead creature receives none. It persists between encounters until depleted or the next beneficial SR/LR, when any old ward ends and entitlement rearms for the next combat, not immediate refill in combat. Repeated initiative does not refill it. This is a distinct spell-only ward, not temp HP: after ordinary defenses and before temp HP, intercept up to its remaining points of actual incoming spell damage in stable component order. Nonspell damage bypasses it. Record ward absorption separately, excluded from actual damage received by the body, Wound/death thresholds and concentration checks; any surviving packet resolves once normally. No transfer, double ledger, HP healing, return on revival or resource proc from ward absorption. Counterspell/dispel cannot target this nonspell passive ward without explicit applicable source permission.
workedCases: A post-defense 20 spell-damage packet consumes 15 ward then passes 5 to temp HP/normal HP.
A sword’s 8 nonspell damage ignores the ward entirely; starting another encounter does not restore spent ward points.

currentPublic.name: Savage Attacker

sourceObject.name: Savage Attacker
sourceObject.description: You fight with primal ferocity.
sourceObject.effect: Once per turn when you roll damage for a melee weapon attack, you can reroll the damage dice and use either total.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Once per turn when you roll damage for your actual melee weapon attack, after seeing that roll but before consequences, reroll the entire eligible native weapon-dice pool once and choose either the complete original total or complete new total. NEW eligible pool includes base weapon dice, their critical copies and expressly additional weapon dice from feats such as Draw Cut, Orcish Fury or Piercer; exclude separate spell/Smite/poison/elemental rider dice and flat modifiers. Preserve each die's native type and apply the chosen corresponding per-type totals, not a pooled total reassigned to a preferred type. Never mix the best die from each pool or reroll only unfavorable dice through this feature. Roll once for each original die identity in the chosen pool, not new attacks or damage events. Maximized/fixed numeric damage has no rolled pool to reroll. Resolve Savage Attacker before Piercer's one-die adjustment if both are used; after selecting a pool you cannot return to a discarded pool to optimize a later modifier. Own and off-turn regular-turn allowances follow the shared cadence.
workedCases: A2d6 pool rolls2+6=8 and rerolls5+1=6. Choose8 or6, never6+5=11.
A separate poison2d6 rider remains its original roll; Savage Attacker does not reroll it just because it accompanied the melee hit.

sourceObject.description: Strength 14+ and melee training support the listed +5% damage per consecutive hit.

sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Track a consecutive direct melee-attack hit chain for each owner during one encounter. Every actual melee attack you make advances the event sequence: a hit on the same current target increases the count; a miss or attack directed at a different target ends the old chain, and a hit on the new target starts a new count1. NEW any intervening nonmelee attack also breaks the chain; movement, spellcasting without attacks and nonattack actions do not. Own/off-turn melee attacks participate, but copies/periodic events do not. Once per turn, before rolling a qualifying hit's damage, add min(PB, prior consecutive hits on that target) as a flat native-type bonus. Only declare when at least one prior hit exists; spending on this hit prevents spending on a later hit that turn. The chain persists across regular turn boundaries but ends on target death/removal, encounter conclusion, or loss of that actual creature identity. Transformation of the same surviving identity retains it if target continuity is real.
workedCases: Three consecutive hits on one foe at PB3 permit choosing+1 on hit2 or+2 on hit3 that turn, not both.
After two hits, a missed opportunity attack breaks the chain. The next melee hit starts at1 and has no prior-hit bonus.

currentPublic.name: Scavenger

sourceObject.name: Scavenger
sourceObject.description: You can find useful items in unlikely places.
sourceObject.effect: You can find basic equipment and supplies in ruins, dungeons, and other locations where others have been.

currentPublic.operationalRules: NEW finite search procedure: choose an accessible previously occupied site and spend thirty active minutes searching one bounded area, such as a room, wreck compartment or campsite. Before the roll the Director records the actual recoverable mundane equipment/supplies, their condition, ownership and access barriers. Make Intelligence (Investigation), DC12 for ordinary scattered remains,15 for concealed useful pieces or20 for heavily obscured remains; a specific site DC takes precedence. On success identify up to1d4 actual item lots from that finite inventory, with a combined reference value at most10gp and combined cargo at most1Load. The die cannot create missing lots: take no more than actually exist and are within those limits. The player chooses which identified lots to retrieve, paying any separate safe-access/removal time; uncollected objects remain in place. These are ordinary catalog-compatible items or usable supplies, not magic loot, a free recipe ingredient classification or converted gp-to-Supply. A larger valuable object can be noticed by the normal search result but is not granted as an extra feat output. Mark searched evidence and removed quantities; another unchanged search of the same area gives no fresh roll or generated inventory. Genuine new access, deposited material or a different bounded area can justify a new attempt.
workedCases: The die gives4 but the site holds only two eligible real lots worth7gp and0.5Load: only those two can be recovered. No third or fourth lot appears.
A found locked chest still requires opening and ownership consequences. Repeating the scavenging roll cannot turn its unknown contents into free mundane supplies.

sourceObject.name: Sentinel
sourceObject.description: You excel at locking down enemies.
sourceObject.effect: When you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, the creature's speed becomes 0 for the rest of the turn.

currentPublic.operationalRules: When your actual opportunity attack hits a creature, set all its current Speed modes to0 for the rest of the actual turn containing that event. NEW the endpoint is that enclosing turn's end, including an actual extra-turn end, not the target's next future turn; outside initiative use the remainder of the current6second interval. The hit qualifies even if damage is0. This overrides ordinary positive Speed additions during the interval and preserves spent movement cost; ending it restores otherwise-current Speed without refunding cost. It stops subsequent voluntary Speed expenditure, but not independently legal forced movement or teleport. A flying creature withSpeed0 follows existing Falling/hover/support rules, not immediate invented fall damage. Disengage still prevents the opportunity trigger. A Reaction attack that is not an opportunity attack, or Combat Casting's replacement spell, does not qualify. No ally-attack trigger, extraReaction or bypass of condition defenses is granted.
workedCases: An opportunity hit during an enemy's movement setsSpeed0 through that enemy turn's end, preventing later ordinary movement.
An independently legal teleport can still move the target; Sentinel does not turn0Speed into a teleport prohibition.

currentPublic.name: Shattering Smash

sourceObject.name: Shattering Smash
sourceObject.description: Strength 16+ supports the listed ability to break an enemy shield or block.
sourceObject.effect: When you hit a creature using a shield or maintaining a physical block, forgo one damage die to force a Strength save. On a failure, its shield bonus or block benefit is suppressed until the start of its next turn.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: On a melee weapon attack hit against a creature receiving an actual wielded shield AC contribution or a sourced current physical-block benefit, before rolling damage forgo one base weapon die under the same pre-critical payment contract as Disarming Blow. NEW save is STR DC8+PB+the actual attack ability modifier. Resolve remaining damage, then on failed save suppress either the chosen shield's entire AC contribution (including its own enhancement) or one selected block benefit through the target's next original regular start. No destruction, durability loss, forced drop or suppression of unrelated item traits; independent magical barriers/unarmored formulas remain. A shield-dependent feat AC bonus is suppressed while its shield cannot supply defensive contribution. Physical block means a named sourced defense actually interposing a held body/object; ordinary armor, cover terrain and taking Dodge do not alone qualify. Same-identity suppression does not multiply, and separate expiries remain. You cannot spend the same die on another rider.

currentPublic.name: Silent Movement

sourceObject.name: Silent Movement
sourceObject.description: Stealth 4+ supports the listed no-penalty movement through difficult terrain.
sourceObject.effect: Nonmagical difficult terrain does not impose disadvantage on your Stealth checks, and moving at half speed allows you to remain silent across ordinary debris.
sourceObject.legacyEffect: No penalty when moving through difficult terrain
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Remove only disadvantage on your Stealth check that an actual rule or stated terrain adjudication assigns because the terrain is nonmagical and difficult. Do not invent a default disadvantage for all difficult terrain. NEW: declare silent-debris movement before any voluntary movement on your turn; outside initiative declare it before the complete continuous traverse. Halve your otherwise current applicable movement Speed for that whole turn or traverse, including the Speed used by Dash, and pay ordinary terrain costs from that reduced budget. Changing movement mode or leaving the debris does not refund that interval's reduction. Your own careful footfalls and disturbed ordinary debris make no revealing sound from that traverse. This is a narrow sound suppression; carried clattering gear, speech, attacks, collisions, collapsing structures and other independent sounds remain. Actual difficult-terrain movement costs and body/load limits remain. Magical terrain's sound or disadvantage is not suppressed by the nonmagical clause. Observers may see, smell or otherwise locate you; use actual Hide/Stealth rules for those senses. The feat does not establish Hidden automatically.
workedCases: Walking Speed 30 becomes 15 for the declared silent turn. Ordinary difficult terrain costs 2 feet per foot, so that budget pays for 7.5 actual feet, or one whole 5-foot tile where whole-tile movement is used. A Dash adds the reduced 15-foot budget, not an unreduced 30.
A silent traverse across pebbles remains plainly visible in a lit corridor. A loudly rattling carried chain is a separate sound source.

currentPublic.name: Silver Tongue

sourceObject.name: Silver Tongue
sourceObject.description: Charisma 14+ supports the listed +5 to persuasion when speaking diplomatically.
sourceObject.effect: Gain +2 on Persuasion checks made through formal diplomacy, negotiation, or mediation.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Add +2 to an actual Persuasion check conducted through diplomacy, negotiation or mediation of a stated agreement, dispute or exchange. NEW: formal describes an acknowledged purposeful exchange with an identifiable request and stakes, not a requirement for court clothing or an official office. The affected party must receive and understand the argument through a legal direct or interpreted channel. Use the social procedure's actual eligibility, DC, stakes, evidence, cost and retry rule. The feat supplies no automatic discount, consent, altered reputation, loyalty, treaty enforcement or permission to ask an impossible favor. A Deception lie, Intimidation threat or unrelated Performance does not receive this Persuasion bonus merely because it occurs in a negotiation. Clothing and other modifiers retain their actual separate qualifications and the shared proposed stacking rule.
workedCases: A clearly stated bargain for a real porter service can qualify for +2 on a required Persuasion check. The bonus does not remove the agreed wage or invent an available porter.
An Intimidation check threatening a guard gets no Silver Tongue bonus, even when described as hard negotiation.

currentPublic.name: Skill Expert

sourceObject.name: Skill Expert
sourceObject.description: You have honed your proficiency with particular skills.
sourceObject.effect: You gain proficiency in one skill and expertise in one skill you're proficient with.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Choose one actual skill in which you lack proficiency and gain it. Then choose one skill in which you are now proficient and lack Expertise; its applicable PB contribution becomes2PB. NEW: the newly chosen skill may be selected for Expertise. Record the two grants separately and preserve their acquisition order. No additional ability increase is inferred from a familiar external feat of the same name. Multiple Expertise sources never produce4PB, and skill Expertise does not automatically apply to an associated tool/crafting check. Choices are permanent unless an actual reviewed retraining procedure applies. If every eligible choice is already satisfied, record that portion exhausted with no extra resource or future floating selection.
workedCases: You gain Medicine proficiency and select Medicine for Expertise in the same acquisition. PB2 contributes4to Medicine checks, once, rather than2+4.
Already having Arcana Expertise means choosing Arcana again adds nothing; choose another eligible proficient skill for the Expertise grant. Smith’s-tools crafting does not inherit Arcana Expertise.

currentPublic.name: Skilled

sourceObject.name: Skilled
sourceObject.description: You gain proficiency in any combination of three skills or tools of your choice.
sourceObject.effect: Gain proficiency in three skills or tools

currentPublic.operationalRules: Choose any combination totaling three distinct eligible skill or tool proficiencies not already possessed. NEW: resolve fixed existing class/background grants first, then these actual choices in order. Any-tool scope includes profiled non-artisan tools such as Fishing tackle, Herbalism kit or thieves’ tools; it does not grant every tool in a kit family. Each primary-trade credential can initialize only its mapped trade at level1/zeroXP, while already higher lawful training remains. No Expertise, ability score, extra PB, formula or physical kit is granted. Choice exhaustion and later duplicates follow the shared rule; a later class/background gain does not freely retarget this historical selection. The feat is not repeatable under this proposal because the source does not say so.

Choosing the same skill three times is not Expertise. A later grant of one selected tool retains both provenance records but still gives one PB contribution and no new free choice.

currentPublic.name: Skulker

sourceObject.name: Skulker
sourceObject.description: You excel at hiding and moving unseen.
sourceObject.effect: You can hide when lightly obscured and missing with a ranged weapon attack doesn't reveal your position.

currentPublic.operationalRules: You may attempt Hide when only lightly obscured, provided an actual source of light obscuration affects that observer's view; use the normal observer-specific Stealth/passive procedure. This is an express permission to try, not automatic Hidden, invisibility or an ability to hide in plainly unobscured sight. When your ranged-class weapon attack misses, suppress the ordinary attack-rule automatic position reveal caused by that missed shot for observers from whom you were Hidden. Do not end your Hidden record merely for the shot's normal firing noise/trajectory. NEW independent clear observation, a successful Search, movement into unobscured sight, communication revealing your position or another actual disclosure can still locate you; they are not negated by missing. A hit reveals normally. Spell misses and thrown melee-class weapons are outside this ranged-weapon clause. It neither improves vision in darkness nor suppresses all evidence permanently.
workedCases: A hidden archer misses from light foliage; the miss alone does not reveal the archer's position.
Stepping into a plainly visible lit doorway afterward still ends Hidden, regardless of the prior miss.

sourceObject.description: Intelligence 16+ supports the listed 10% chance to redirect hostile spell.
sourceObject.effect: Once per long rest, when targeted by a single-target hostile spell, roll a d20. On 16 or higher, redirect it to another legal target within its original range; otherwise gain advantage on the saving throw.
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: Once LR, NEW spend a Reaction when a hostile pending spell has selected you as its sole creature target, after ordinary cast interruptions but before its attack/save/effect resolution. It must be an actual single-target payload, not one target remaining from an area or multi-target mode. Roll an unmodifiedd 20;16–20 redirects, preserving this explicit 25%procedure over legacy 10%. On success choose a different legal creature under the original spell’s actual target restrictions, range/line measured from the original origin, personally perceived by you where necessary; the original caster remains owner and supplies all stats/choices. Recheck legality, then use fresh original attack/save procedure against that new target; nothing resolves against you. If no legal new target exists, or on 1–15, the spell continues against you with advantage on each actual initial save it requires; no save is invented for an attack/automatic spell. Use/Reaction remain spent. A redirected/reflected/copy packet cannot be redirected again by this family or Spell Reflection. Protected/self-only/source-specific exclusions remain.

currentPublic.name: Spell Echo Chamber

sourceObject.name: Spell Echo Chamber
sourceObject.description: Your spells can affect a wider area through magical resonance.
sourceObject.effect: Next spell affects area twice

currentPublic.operationalRules:
Keep total character level10. The original sentence “Next spell affects area twice” has no complete trigger,budget or geometry, so all following limits are NEW. Once per beneficial Long Rest, use a Bonus Action to prime one Echo Chamber for one minute. It applies to the next eligible spell you legally commit in that interval; a spell with no qualifying area does not consume the priming but the clock continues. Repriming is impossible until the use returns. An eligible spell directly establishes a finite,explicit cone,line,cube,circle or sphere of spell effects, instantaneous or sustained; it does not create extra creatures,objects,portals,physical inventory or paid item bodies merely because their spell has a listed area. A solely single-target,touch-only or indeterminate-area spell is ineligible.

At that eligible cast’s commitment, declare two full placements of the same actual area geometry, each independently legal under the original casting range/origin/line rules. Self-origin cones/lines must both originate at the actual caster; choose their separate orientations, not a second caster. A self-centered emanation retains its one actual center, so a coincident duplicate grants no wider footprint. A point-area spell may use two legal points. Spend only the spell’s ordinary cast costs, with one Dissonance/Refrain update, interruption window and concentration obligation; the feat use was already spent at priming and its prime is consumed at commitment even if countered.

Both placements have full native size/effect; NEW a creature or physical target included by both is resolved only once for each actual native spell trigger event. Roll shared native damage once for the combined simultaneous application, then resolve each distinct target’s save/defenses. No overlapping double damage, duplicate save or control record. For sustained zones, keep one actual spell identity and its existing per-target trigger budget across both areas; moving through both cannot reset a same-turn/round/cast allowance. Later pulses occur at the original spell’s real deadlines, and a genuine different native trigger remains distinct only where the original card already permits it. Concentration loss or ordinary ending ends both. If the source allows one area-movement command, NEW move at most one placement with that one command, not both for free; each remains subject to all actual control ranges. A dispel selecting this single ongoing cast ends its whole duplicated area application unless the original spell explicitly defines independently separable effects. The feat adds no second spell, second payload budget or half-strength Echo Spell rule.
workedCases: A qualifying20-foot-radius spell is placed at two legal origins. A creature in both rolls its one native save and receives the shared damage result once; a creature only in the second is also a normal eligible target.

A sustained damaging area’s native once-per-turn entry limit remains one across both placements. Losing the one concentration ends both, and moving one area with an Action does not move the other for free.

sourceObject.name: Spell Penetration
sourceObject.description: Your spells are particularly effective against magical defenses.
sourceObject.effect: +2 bonus to spell attack rolls against targets with spell resistance

currentPublic.operationalRules:
Retain total character level5and actual personal spellcasting. NEW bounded target predicate: at the instant of your personal spell attack roll, the target must have a real currently active source explicitly named Spell Resistance or Magic Resistance, or a rule granting general advantage on saves against spells as a category. The supplied Shaman Bloodcaller Spell Resistance qualifies through its actual active save-advantage card; its lack of an attack-defense number does not erase the feat’s printed attack bonus. Specific fire resistance,highAC,cover,condition-only save advantage or War Caster’s concentration advantage does not qualify by itself. An inactive,suppressed or exhausted conditional defense does not qualify.

Against such a target, add+2to your genuine spell attack roll, once for this feat identity. This does not negate its defense,lowerAC,change saveDC,aid a Counterspell/Dispel ability check,turn a save into an attack or ignore immunity. A separately actual general flat spell-attack feat bonus can combine under the proposed feat family unless its own source says otherwise. Apply the predicate from real game state without giving the player an extra identification scan: the Director can adjudicate a hidden qualifying record without disclosing its name or inferential reason. Companion attacks merely using your spell attack modifier are not your personal spell attack for this feat.
workedCases: A Shaman with active Spell Resistance is targeted by your actual spell attack. Add2to your attack; its ordinary save advantage remains relevant to other actual saves and is not removed.
A target resistant only tofire grants no Spell Penetration bonus. A Counterspell check against an actual spell from a resistant caster is still an ability check and gains no+2.

currentPublic.name: Spell Scribe

sourceObject.name: Spell Scribe
sourceObject.description: Arcana 4+ and Intelligence 14+ support the listed faster, reduced-cost scroll copying.
sourceObject.effect: Copying a spell or scroll takes half the normal active time and costs 25 percent fewer mundane materials. Rare inks and unique components are unchanged.
sourceObject.legacyEffect: Copy scrolls faster and at reduced cost
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules: First identify an actually authorized copying procedure and the exact spell or scroll, legal source access, rank, language/notation, ability/tool requirements, facility and recipient record. Reduce only that actor's eligible copying active time to one half and mundane-material quantities to three quarters; rare inks and unique components are unchanged. NEW: apply the strongest eligible reduction separately to each time/material category, rather than multiplying overlapping reductions. Wizard Spell Scribing therefore supplies the same half-time factor and its better half-cost factor for its own qualifying copying; owning both gives neither quarter time nor a second material discount. Convert to minutes and round the final active time upward to a whole minute. For divisible mundane inputs retain exact quantities; for indivisible items round required remaining units upward; a listed aggregate gp expense rounds upward to the next cp. Separately identify rare/unique inputs before applying a discount to a mixed bill. No classification from absence: an unitemized ambiguous special-ink bill must be resolved by its source procedure before a discount is claimed. Level-up free additions remain free. Matrix preparation, reconstructing unknown text from memory, formula research and copying an ordinary craft formula are not spell/scroll copying. A usable scroll can be duplicated only under a separately authorized scroll-production procedure; the feat supplies no procedure or item effect.
workedCases: A legal copying task costs 120 minutes, 40 gp mundane supplies and 10 gp separately identified rare ink: this feat gives 60 minutes, 30 gp mundane and the unchanged 10 gp rare ink.
A Wizard also owning Spell Scribing uses that feature's half time and half eligible cost, not 120×0.5×0.5. Four indivisible mundane sheets become three; one required sheet still remains one.

currentPublic.name: Spell Sniper

sourceObject.name: Spell Sniper
sourceObject.description: You have learned techniques to enhance your spells.
sourceObject.prerequisite: Ability to cast at least one spell
sourceObject.effect: When you cast a spell that requires a ranged attack roll, the spell's range is doubled.

currentPublic.operationalRules:
Require an actual acquired ability to cast a spell. When you personally cast a spell whose own procedure requires a ranged spell attack, double its finite positive printed casting range for that cast. NEW this is a casting-range modifier, not a doubling of radius,cone,length,speed,companion command range,secondary-target spacing or maintained-control distance. Self,Touch,unlimited and a creature’s independent ranged attack after summoning do not qualify. A spell requiring only a save or a melee spell attack does not qualify merely because its narration travels through the air. A spell granting a separate ordinary weapon attack is not converted into a ranged spell attack by this feat.

The actual target/origin must remain legal within that doubled casting range and under line,visibility and source exclusions. A spell with an independently stated shorter later control/attack distance retains that distance; this feat changes only its initial range. Use the actual chosen placement’s printed range, not the catalog’s maximum header from another mode. Apply the doubling once; proposed Metamagic Reach adds its30feet afterward. No cover ignoring,extra cantrip,expanded critical or generic accuracy bonus is granted.
workedCases: A genuine ranged spell attack with printed60-foot casting range can target at120feet if ordinary line/target rules permit. A20-foot effect radius remains20feet.
A summoned creature’s30-foot ranged attack stays30feet. Casting a self-origin beam whose range isSelfdoes not invent a numeric range to double.

currentPublic.name: Spellweave

sourceObject.name: Spellweave
sourceObject.description: Wisdom 14+ supports the listed stacking of minor buffs onto the next spell.
sourceObject.effect: When you cast a spell that grants a minor buff, you may hold that buff until the end of your next turn and apply it to the next spell you cast instead. Only one buff may be held.
sourceObject.legacyEffect: Stack minor buffs onto next spell
sourceObject.source: Completed from the existing feat draft corpus on 2026-08-05; playable wording supplied, final balance pass still required.

currentPublic.operationalRules:
NEW use the finite three-spell minor-buff table below: personally cast Guidance, Resistance or True Strike with yourself as the otherwise legal recipient. At its completion hold that entire one-use buff instead of receiving it normally; only one held record, replacing loses the old. Original costs, cast history and earlier deadline remain, with an additional deadline at your next future regular end. The next actual spell you commit consumes/attaches the record automatically, even if countered or unsuitable; no indefinite skipping. Guidance adds its one 1d4 only to one actual ability/task check made by that next spell, declared before rolling; Resistance adds its one 1d4 only to one actual concentration save maintaining that next spell; True Strike grants advantage only on that next spell’s first actual spell attack. They create no check/save/attack. The attachment expires at the original held deadline or actual spell end, whichever first, even if unused. Current one-bonus-die/advantage rules apply. A copied buff, borrowed duplicate or another Spellweave cannot be held; no duration/resource/HP/stat transfer or new cast.
The three selected current buffs are non-concentration spells. Holding/attaching their one-use benefit adds no concentration requirement and does not change that source fact. There is still only one held Spellweave record and each original deadline/cost/history; no newly invented check or save may redeem it.
workedCases: Held Guidance attaches to a legal next Counterspell and can add 1d4 to its actual counter check.
Held True Strike consumed by a next spell with no attack produces no benefit and cannot wait for a third cast.
