unchangedReviewedRecord.operationalRules:
## Soul Cage feat — Magic; level8+ and (Lifeleech **or** actual spellcasting ability)

On acquisition, lock one actually possessed spellcasting source/ability as this feat's DC provider. Agony uses that source's current normal spell-save DC. No freely switchable DC ability or general retraining is created.

**Shared Soul Charges:** each owner has one persistent pool0..3, shared with Lifeleech. A charge is a soul **spark/residue**, not custody of the whole soul. It neither prevents resurrection nor replaces/removes Soul Bind. The ordinary Soul Cage spell is a separate rank6/13RP spell awaiting its own operational review. Soulrender's separate whole-soul ritual unlock still requires actually binding the soul of a living named enemy; residue cannot satisfy it.

At an eligible hostile soul-bearing creature's actual death within30ft, with perception and legal line of effect, Soul Cage permits immediate optional capture with no Action or Reaction. A discrete physical black crystal must actually be possessed and available. Lifeleech collection is automatic and needs no crystal. Owning both never gives two charges for the same death.

Each owner permanently records the exact death event as evaluated, including ineligible events. There is no later corpse rescan after moving closer, gaining a feat/crystal or improving perception. For an eligible event, also reserve the immutable body for that owner's current completed-long-rest epoch. Declining or being at full capacity consumes that entitlement; there is no latent fourth charge. A new real death after resurrection is a new event, but the same body cannot supply the owner again in the same epoch. A future completed rest can permit a future new death, never the old corpse. Different owners evaluate independently.

Created/generated farming bodies and immutable object-origin transformed creatures are ineligible. Soul status otherwise follows actual source/canon or Director adjudication; this feat does not declare every undead/construct category soulless. Death/root/body identities persist through forms.

Charges live on the owner and do not decay automatically. Losing/destroying/transferring the crystal transfers or erases **zero** charges; Soul Cage capture/spending is unavailable without another actual legal black crystal. Another feat owner can use the transferred physical crystal for their own pool. There is no invented price, attunement, HP, durability or crystal charge capacity. During one uninterrupted quiet minute handling the crystal, you may voluntarily dissipate owned charges; this does nothing to any deceased soul.

**Shield:** Bonus Action; pay1 Soul Charge; one legal ally within30ft, including yourself; roll2d8 temporary HP with default lifetime. Pay before strongest-only comparison. An equal/stronger old shield does not refund the charge or Bonus Action.

**Agony Lance:** Action; pay2 Soul Charges; one perceived legal creature within60ft; CON save against the locked provider's current DC. Deal3d8 necrotic damage, half rounded down on success, then ordinary defenses/Core apply once. This is feat damage owned by you, not a spell, RP expenditure or spellcasting trigger.

The target also gains one **Agony healing-suppression family** record until the next committed ordinary HP-healing event with positive pre-reduction potential, or one elapsed minute. That next healing receives an exact×1/2 factor in the canonical healing pipeline. Save success or necrotic immunity affects damage but does not remove this separate rider. Multiple Agony Lances never multiply to1/4: a new paid application refreshes the single endpoint to `max(old expiry, new application+60s)` and retains contributor history.

Consume the suppression on the first applicable committed healing event even if a stronger arithmetic branch wins or actual healing is later capped/prohibited. Suppressed/inapplicable records do not apply or consume; absolute time continues. Temporary HP, stabilization, resurrection, prevention and maximum-HP changes are not ordinary HP healing and do not consume it. Removal requires an exact source capable of removing this magical suppression/debuff; generic cure is insufficient.

**NEW:** prerequisite parsing, residue identity, shared resource/death transaction, conduit role, activations/ranges/DC and the exact healing-suppression conversion. Original source IDs and relationships remain distinct.

Require actual spellcasting AND (Nature proficiency OR a separately established Spellcraft credential). Spellcraft is not an Arcana alias; if absent, use the Nature alternative. Once per beneficial SR/LR, an Action places a fixed 15 ft radius Static Field at a perceived point within 60 ft and line of effect, requiring concentration for up to one minute. It affects all creatures, including allies: first actual entry or regular start inside per target per numbered round deals 1d6 lightning automatically. Placement covering a creature counts as entry once. While inside an active field, creatures have disadvantage on DEX saves, ending immediately on exit; actual immunities/suppression apply. Outdoors during an established storm, choose a 20 ft radius at creation. A separate once-SR/LR Action, Stormstep, teleports you up to 30 ft to a visible fitting unoccupied space with line of effect. Every other creature within 5 ft of arrival makes a DEX save against your actual casting DC for 1d8 thunder, half on success. NEW select the actual owned casting route at acquisition for both feat activations. Your afterimage supplies half cover until your next regular start only when the geometric ray from the incoming effect origin to your new position passes through your previous occupied space; it is not a solid object or general AC bonus. During an actual outdoor storm, your lightning spells also ignore half cover, but not stronger cover. These activations are nonspell magical feat techniques; they do not create weather, RP or extra casting resources.
NEW storm-size choice is fixed at creation, as this proposal specifies:20ft requires actual outdoor-storm premises at that placement. A later weather change does not enlarge or shrink the placed field; suppression, concentration and its original minute deadline still end it. The separate half-cover benefit checks the actual outdoor-storm predicate when each lightning spell attack resolves. These are source-authoring completions, not permission to interpret the named storm’s setting origin.

currentPublic.operationalRules: At your original regular-turn end, bank at most one genuinely unused NORMAL allowance: your wholly unspent movement budget, ordinary free object interaction, or unused ordinary Bonus Action. You must be conscious, able to act and actually possess it; prohibited, extra, borrowed, banked, readied or generated allowances cannot fund a token. sourceObject.description: Roots, thorns, and spore-mines—you sow violence that waits patiently to bloom. Prestige lineage: Verdant Animist. completed from the existing development record.)
sourceObject.effect: Your conjured flora count as magical traps. Enemies moving through a seedling's square must succeed on a Dexterity save or suffer its effect (damage, restraint, or poison). You can detonate one seedling as a bonus action for a Bloom Burst (10-foot area, 2d6 damage, type chosen at conjuring).

sourceObject.legacyEffect: Your conjured flora count as magical traps. Enemies moving through a seedling's square must succeed on a Dexterity save or suffer its effect (damage, restraint, or poison). currentPublic.operationalRules:
Conjure Flora OR Verdant Bond qualifies for acquisition, but this feat supplies no missing plants. NEW only actual Conjure Flora profiles below qualify until another source is reviewed. At creation optionally arm a plant’s square as a magical trap using its fixed mode/burst type. Each meaningful hostile’s first actual entry in that square per numbered round, including forced entry but not plant placement, makes DEX save against flora DC; failure applies the profile’s trap result, success none. A legal trigger commits the owner’s shared offensive-companion allowance even on a save; if already spent by a command/other trap, no new trap activation occurs that round. One entrance cannot multiply across plants. Plants are visible, not automatically hidden: Action INT(Investigation) vs flora DC identifies an armed mode; Action DEX with actual thieves’ tools vs same DC disarms one trap without destroying its body, failure gives no automatic explosion. Alternatively, BA consumes one active plant within 60 ft you perceive with line of effect for a 10 ft-radius Bloom Burst at its space: all creatures DEX save,2d6 fixed piercing/poison damage, half success. Same offensive allowance; body ends before burst, cannot also command, and never refunds creation.
NEW phase exception is explicit: its first eligible hostile-entry attack may occur on that actual entry outside the ordinary attached phase, but spends the same owner-round offensive companion allowance immediately. Its paid burst likewise spends that allowance; neither can occur when it is already spent. Placement itself is not an entry-trigger unless this exact procedure expressly says so. General Conjure Flora commands retain their attached phase, shared Bonus Action and sensory channel.
workedCases: Forced hostile entry can trigger a plant, but another plant cannot produce a second offensive outcome after the group allowance is spent that round.
Detonation consumes the actual plant even if every creature saves. An expired plant cannot be detonated.

sourceObject.name: Trapsetter
sourceObject.description: Tripwire, caltrop, and charge—the ground remembers your name and bites when asked. Prestige lineage: Sapper. completed from the existing development record.)
sourceObject.prerequisite: Proficiency in Engineering or Disable Device
sourceObject.effect: You can set a mechanical trap as a bonus action (once per short rest per trap type: snare, caltrop field, or spring-loaded charge). Traps may stun, burn, or slow on a failed save (DC 8 + proficiency + Intelligence modifier). You gain advantage on checks to spot hidden traps and tunnels within 30 feet. When a creature triggers a trap you placed, you may use your reaction to move up to half your speed without provoking opportunity attacks from that creature, repositioning behind cover or into a prepared kill-zone.

currentPublic.operationalRules:
Require Engineering proficiency or the proposed mechanical Disable Device/thieves’-tools credential. NEW three closed prepared-kit options use genuine physical parts and no invented recipe/craft XP: snare (5gp reference,2lb cord/spring/anchor), caltrop field (the actual ordinary20-caltrop source bag, preserving its price/weight), and spring-loaded charge (25gp reference,3lb trigger body plus actual prepared combustible filling). Availability and assembly are real: obtain a genuinely prepared kit from an actual provider, or spend30active minutes with suitable mechanical tools and the same actual parts, DC12 INT/Engineering or DEX/thieves’-tools, using Core binary task outcome. Failure consumes time and expendable cord/filling, retaining only real recoverable frame/metal parts; no free complete kit. The new reference prices are complete kit references, not added again to their component prices. No ordinary Rune or Tinkering formula is silently renamed one of these three options.

Place one held/accessible prepared kit in a real stable unoccupied5-foot ground square within5feet. Normally this feat procedure takes an Action; once per Short Rest for each of the three types, you may use a Bonus Action instead, spending that type’s separate quick-placement allowance. NEW one armed trap of each type per setter; a new enhanced trap of that type cannot arm until the old trap has actually been safely disarmed, discharged, collected or destroyed through a lawful physical event. Merely arming a replacement or changing custody cannot remotely disable an existing trap. Ordinary unenhanced caltrop placements retain their own item rule. It arms at your next original regular-turn start, or after six elapsed seconds outside initiative, preserving the same deadline across mode changes. SnapshotDC8+PB+INT modifier at placement. For snare and charge, the first actual grounded creature entering from outside, including an ally, forced movement or teleport arrival, triggers once; an existing occupant, flying above it, or replayed movement is not another entry. The target makesDEXsave against the storedDC. On failure: snare givesStunned until the target’s next regular-turn end; charge deals2d6fire in that same event with no ongoing Burn; caltrop field uses the reviewed ordinary caltrop failure effect of1piercing, stopping remaining movement that turn and-10walkingSpeed until1HPhealing or an Action removes the caltrop. The caltrop slow is one shared same-area effect, not a new Slow condition, and moving at halfSpeed still avoids its save as under its actual item rule. Success avoids the trap’s feat effect. NEW snare and charge discharge after that first eligible trigger regardless of result; surviving actual metal/body can be recovered, but rearming requires a new prepared kit procedure and actual expendables. A caltrop field remains physically present and hazardous after an entry or successful save. Each actual new entry follows its stored feat DC and ordinary caltrop procedure, including half-Speed avoidance; an unchanged standing position is not another entry. Preserve all actual placed, embedded, removed and recovered pieces; no embedded piece exists simultaneously in the field or returns twice. Loss of actual coverage or stock can reduce the hazard only through the physical source record, not automatic first-trigger discharge. The field continues occupying the setter’s one enhanced-caltrop allowance until it is physically cleared. A charge consumes its filling; this does not duplicate its frame. Placement speed does not shorten preparation or refill after transfer.

The exposed snare/charge assembly isAC15/5HP; caltrops retain their actual ordinary physical pieces. An Action with safe reach disarms your own accessible trap. Another creature that has detected it can spend an Action with actual appropriate tools onDCequal to storedDC using INT/Engineering or DEX/thieves’-tools; failure triggers it only if that actual manipulation enters its working trigger, not arbitrarily against a remote observer. Hidden placement requires actual concealment: record one real setter DEX/Stealth check opposed by the actual search/passive-perception procedure, without granting invisibility. Once visible, ordinary physical removal/destruction still follows actual reach/safety and object rules. A snare/charge whose necessary mechanism is moved, Broken or disconnected becomes disarmed and needs real rearming; a cover prevents its trigger only while physically effective. Moving or covering some caltrops does not magically remove the remainder. NEW safe collection of an accessible unoccupied caltrop square requires one active minute with actual hands, tools/protection as necessary and a real receiver; retain the count and condition of the pieces actually collected. Unsafe manipulation follows the actual hazard. Reconstruction never duplicates stock or the type’s spent quick-placement use.

You have advantage on actual checks to spot hidden traps or tunnel evidence within30feet, not automatic sight through walls or knowledge that a tunnel exists. On a real trigger of any trap you personally placed, after its immediate effect resolves and if you are still capable of taking a Reaction and can perceive the triggering creature within30feet, you may spend that Reaction to move up to half your current applicable Speed. Pay ordinary terrain/mode costs from this distinct movement budget, respect speed0/restraints and actual paths. This movement provokes no opportunity attack from that triggering creature; other creatures’ normal opportunity attacks remain. You may use real cover or a real prepared kill-zone at the destination, but the feat creates neither. One trigger event permits at most one Reaction; copies, already discharged traps and additional targets of one blast are not new triggers.
The snare’s Stunned application uses the existing source/target/encounter hard-denial eligibility and immunity ledger; rearming or changing trap IDs does not reset it. If barred, no substitute damage or condition is awarded. The charge’s2d6fire is immediate damage, not a separate Burn condition. For assembly, resolve Core task degrees/natural shifts and collapse to success/failure; the basic-dismantling no-natural-shift exception does not apply. All other packet body, price and material quantities remain explicitly NEW authoring values, not previously catalogued source statistics.
workedCases: A quick-placed snare is moved before arming and loses its actual trigger arrangement. The quick-placement use remains spent. Another enhanced snare cannot erase an older still-armed snare remotely; that older one must physically cease to be armed.

A caltrop field is entered twice by different creatures. Both qualifying entries resolve the persistent hazard; the first success or failure does not clear it. Actual embedded/removed pieces are tracked once. After a nearby charge trigger, the setter’s paid half-Speed Reaction movement avoids only that triggering creature’s opportunity attack and creates no cover.

sourceObject.prerequisite: Constitution 15+, Necrotic Affinity or Dark Fortitude
sourceObject.effect: You have resistance to necrotic and poison damage. Once per long rest, when you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you rise at 1 hit point at the start of your next turn with temporary necrotic bonuses (+2 damage for 1 minute).

currentPublic.operationalRules: Require Constitution 15 and actually owned Necrotic Affinity or Dark Fortitude, using their exact feat IDs. Gain resistance to necrotic and poison damage. NEW delayed-recovery procedure: once per completed long rest, after an actual positive-to-zero damage/loss event finishes its Core Instant Death, Wound and death processing and leaves you living at zero, you may commit the use to that real dying/Stable episode without an Action or Reaction. NEW this trigger choice is permitted despite Unconscious/Incapacitated caused by this just-completed drop to0; it does not require an impossible conscious Reaction. No earlier corpse, unrelated historical0HP episode or lethal event qualifies. Record a recovery deadline at the start of your next original regular turn, preserving its virtual marker if initiative changes. At that deadline, before the normal death save, if you are still living at zero in that same episode, attempt direct state recovery to 1 HP. Broad HP-gain prohibition blocks the point; it does not create stability or refund the use. Earlier positive healing closes the pending episode and cancels this later recovery without reducing HP; actual death cancels it and cannot be reversed. On actual successful recovery, NEW: gain a one-elapsed-minute rider adding 2 necrotic damage once to each genuine personally owned damaging attack/spell/feature event, before target defenses. Apply it once to a shared area roll/event, with each target resolving its own defenses; a mixed-type packet does not gain it per component. Fixed damage and actual ongoing source ticks can qualify, but copied/reflected damage, another creature's actions and newly invented split packets do not. The flat +2 is not doubled by critical hits. It is this feat's damage component, not ordinary spell damage for Lifeleech, and creates no new spell, hit, payment, resource event or damage root; it cannot recursively trigger itself. Direct recovery does not remove Wounds, Prone or an independent cause of Unconsciousness. It ends on its deadline or your actual death and does not stack with itself. Missing this delayed recovery or being killed before it never becomes a later corpse wake-up.

currentPublic.operationalRules:
Require character 6 AND (Stormcaller OR Lightning Affinity); preserve the named pact/plane story undecided. Once per personal noncopy lightning spell’s initial resolution, choose one additional creature within 15 ft of one original recipient, perceived with line of effect from that recipient. It must satisfy original creature eligibility and not already be targeted by that cast. Deal only half the selected original native lightning packet before defenses, rounded down; use the original DC/save ability for a fresh save or original attack bonus for a fresh attack, with original half/none on success. No other riders, new cast or chain from a chain. After one entire original start-to-next-start interval without any position change, gain Eye of the Tempest: resistance to all damage and+2 to one immediate native packet/shared roll of each personal spell until the following regular start. Any movement, teleport or forced displacement ends Eye immediately; riding a moving mount counts as movement. Repeated stationary intervals may renew without stacking. Separately, once LR use Action for a 30 ft-long 5 ft-wide lightning line: all creatures DEX save,4d6 lightning half success. DC=8+PB+one actual casting ability selected at acquisition, or INT if no casting source. The line is a magical nonspell feat technique, with noRPpool or weather creation.
The Eye bonus is+2 to one immediate native packet/shared roll of each personal spell as printed here; it is not limited to lightning spells. Half-damage chaining uses a resolved native lightning packet, not an attack that missed, a reflected/copy result, external rider or new target-independent resource event. Existing stance, terrain, body and actual stationary interval rules remain.
workedCases: Native 17 lightning damage gives a chain base of 8 before the new target’s save and defenses; that child cannot chain again.
Forced movement prevents the stationary interval. Riding a moving mount is not stationary.

currentPublic.operationalRules: After your personally cast noncopy spell deals positive resolved damage, optionally apply one Agony record to one living damaged target, once per owner/target/numbered round. Reapplication refreshes one profile without stacked dice. It deals 1d4 necrotic at the next three original target regular-start markers; a CON save against the generating cast DC at each affected regular end, including a current turn if applicable, ends it. The final third scheduled pulse ends the record after damage; no extra ending save afterward. It is a magical ongoing wound, not Core Wound, maximum HP injury or Bleeding by name. NEW a legal positive-potential magical heal or Action Medicine vs source DC ends it; suppressed records remain curable. While active, disadvantage applies only to actual existing CON saves to regain HP and actual saves against resurrection effects; no such save is invented. Death suspends living damage, retaining only the unexpired record tied to that exact death instance until the original third-start deadline; missed pulses are consumed, never backlogged. A legal revival closes that corpse-specific resurrection rider and retains only any still-future living pulse schedule until cured/expired. This grants no resurrection block or permission. Secondary ticks cannot create further Agony, copies, lifesteal or resource procs. Any independent Necrotic Affinity seal needs its own real fatal-root predicate.
workedCases: The first 1d4 pulse resolves at the target’s regular start; a successful CON save at its regular end removes the remaining pulses.
